Mayfield tossed 26 touchdowns (way down from 41 in 2024) and severely lacked upside, managing only four top-10 fantasy weeks. Granted, the 31-year-old was not fully healthy throughout the season and did still finish in the top 10 at the position in key categories, including passing yards, passing TDs and rushing yards. With a solid supporting cast and Zac Robinson as playcaller, Mayfield has some rebound potential and does just enough with his legs to make him an appealing QB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Reed will look to make more of his opportunities as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Reed struggled even with seven targets in a loss to the Vikings, logging just three catches for 20 yards. The fourth-year playmaker could start to slip into a WR3 role if he continues to play similarly, but luckily there appears to be plenty of targets to go around in the short term. Reed will face a New York defense that ranked middle-of-the-pack against wide receivers this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jayden Reed's status is up in the air as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Reed was carted off the field after injuring his back on the first drive of Week 2, which in itself makes it unlikely that he'll be rushed back for a TNF matchup. The fourth-year playmaker's absence would give Matthew Golden even more looks, with Skyy Moore and Bo Melton slotting in as supplementary options for Jordan Love. If Reed somehow does play, he'll face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jayden Reed is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Packers take on the Falcons. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he hasn't seen the field since. The fourth-year wide receiver also has no current return timeline. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jayden Reed will not play in Week 5 as the Packers play the Bears. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he'll now require season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

player.seasonOutlook: Reed began his NFL career with a pair of top-30 fantasy campaigns, but the Green Bay slot receiver was limited to only seven appearances last season due to injury. Even when active, Reed wasn't as effective as in years past, averaging 6.9 fantasy PPG and finding the end zone once (Week 1). This comes after the 2023 second-round pick produced 75 touches, 900-plus yards and seven-plus touchdowns in each of his first two seasons. The 26-year-old signed a contract extension in April and will battle the likes of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Savion Williams for targets this season. While he'll likely hit for the occasional solid game, his limited usage (career-high 18% target share) will put a cap on his fantasy upside. He's barely in the flex conversation in PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.5: Tank Dell (knee) is expected to have his practice window opened ahead of the Texans' Week 5 road game against the Titans. The 2023 third-round pick hasn't played since sustaining a significant knee injury in Week 16 of the 2024 season. Dell is currently on injured reserve and will likely take some time to ramp up. He's unlikely to return in Week 5 against Tennessee, but forward-looking fantasy managers should take notice of Dell's impending return, as he averaged 55 receiving yards and scored 10 TDs in 25 games prior to his injury.

player.seasonOutlook: Dell is on the comeback trail after suffering a devastating knee injury late in 2024 that cost him the entire 2025 season. It was a tough break for the 2023 third-round pick, who finished 18th among receivers in fantasy PPG as a rookie. While he wasn't quite as productive the next season, he was on pace for career highs in catches and yardage. The undersized Dell is certainly a question mark off the major injury, but, with Jayden Higgins out for the 2026 season, he has a path back to a role behind Nico Collins at some point this year. The 26-year-old will begin on injured reserve, but he'll be a fine end-of-bench stash once activated.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Washington's volume was limited in his NFL debut, but he was productive, gaining 41 rushing yards on seven carries in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins. The quality of his opposition needs to be taken into account, but it was still a strong showing from the 2026 fourth-round pick. Lead back Ashton Jeanty had a huge game, proving he was fully recovered from a preseason ankle injury, but if he has trouble staying on the field, Washington appears very capable of stepping into a larger role. He'll face a tough matchup in Week 2 against a Chargers defense that ranked second in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Washington hasn't seen much action to begin his NFL career, getting 10 carries through the Raiders' first two games and turning them into 48 yards. He also failed to bring in his only target. Ashton Jeanty is locked into the top spot in the backfield and has 54 touches, third in the league behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Kenneth Walker, and unless he gets hurt, Washington's workload figures to be limited. The rookie will look to take advantage of the chances he does get in Week 3 against a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Washington showed off his big-play potential in the Raiders' Week 3 win over the Saints, turning one of his five carries into a 36-yard touchdown. The rookie fourth-round pick hasn't logged big volume behind Ashton Jeanty, but that could begin to change if the starting RB continues to average just 3.3 yards per carry, compared to Washington's 6.8 mark. Until his workload ticks up, Washington will be little more than a dart throw or bench stash for fantasy rosters. He'll face a Kansas City defense in Week 4 that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Washington failed to produce another big play in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, managing only 18 rushing yards on nine carries while catching one of two targets for minus-1 yard. Ashton Jeanty continues to struggle on the ground, but Washington hasn't yet shown enough consistency to be any kind of threat to his workload on early downs. The rookie is averaging 5.0 yards on his first 24 NFL carries, though, well clear of Jeanty's 3.4 mark, so volume could begin to tilt his way a little more if that trend continues. Washington will try to break free in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that ranked 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Washington was selected by the Raiders in the fourth round of April's draft. He's a big back with terrific speed who lit up the combine with a 4.33 40-yard dash at 6-foot-1, 223 pounds (127 speed score), while also checking in with the longest arms in this rookie RB class. His collegiate efficiency wasn't very good during stops in Buffalo and New Mexico State, but it was better in 2025 -- his lone season at Arkansas -- as he averaged 6.41 yards per carry and 3.62 yards after contact, both of which rank seventh or better in this RB class. He might not be much of an option in the passing game, as his career 4.2 yards per target is the worst in this RB class, but his traits make him an intriguing prospect. Washington will open his career as a clear No. 2 option behind Ashton Jeanty, which makes him an intriguing end-of-bench insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road to face the Patriots in Week 2. He finished Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 win versus the Falcons 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-2 on PATs. Boswell's first miss of the season was from 56 yards out, but he was able to connect from 43 and 28 yards. The Steelers have several talented players on offense, but until they prove they can consistently put up 24-28 points a week, Boswell may not generate enough scoring opportunities to warrant a roster spot.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Boswell and the Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3. The 12th-year kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Both of Boswell's attempts came from 50-plus yards out, and he's now 1-for-3 from that distance and 3-for-5 overall through two outings in 2026. He'll look to get back on track this Sunday versus a Cincinnati defense allowing 16.5 points per game, tied for eighth.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Boswell and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He made all three of his field-goal attempts and went 3-for-3 on PATs during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. It was Boswell's first perfect outing through three games, and his 33-yard kick just before the two-minute warning gave the Steelers the lead for good. He'll look to stay hot against Cleveland's 18th-ranked scoring defense, which is allowing 23.7 points per game thus far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Boswell and the Steelers return home to take on the Colts in Week 5. He finished Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4 converting one of two field-goal attempts while connecting on his lone extra-point try. Boswell's miss came from 48 yards out, and he's now 1-for-4 on kicks equal to or longer than that across four games in 2026. He'll aim to bounce back versus an Indianapolis defense giving up 26.0 points per contest, which ranks 21st in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brenton Strange was one of four Jaguars to catch a touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence in the season-opening win over the Browns, and the starting tight end should remain involved in the Week 2 game plan against the Broncos. The Broncos excelled at defending wide receivers last season but gave up the ninth-most receiving yards to TEs. Strange is a decent fantasy option in multi-TE formats or those with a tight end premium. However, with many mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, Strange is tough to trust as a starter in standard single-TE leagues. Strange has exceeded 61 receiving yards just once since the start of last season while scoring four TDs in 13 appearances over that span.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brenton Strange was a non-factor during the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver, but that was the case for every member of Jacksonville's passing game except for Parker Washington, who accounted for more than half of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards. It won't be easy for Strange to bounce back in Week 3 against the Patriots, who are allowing just 8.0 points per game and have limited TEs to seven catches for 52 yards this season. There are likely better Week 3 options.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brenton Strange remains a complementary piece in Jacksonville's passing game heading into a Week 4 road game against the Bengals. He's locked in atop the Jaguars' TE depth chart, but Strange has just seven catches for 72 yards and a TD on 10 targets in three games-numbers elite options at his position often reach in one game. The Bengals have allowed 23 catches (third-most) and 299 yards (second-most) to TEs, so Strange has more fantasy appeal than usual in Week 4 and is a viable option in multi-TE or TE-premium formats. Even the favorable matchup isn't enough to propel him into the starting range in most one-TE leagues.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brenton Strange became the latest TE to take advantage of a Bengals defense that has allowed the most yards in the league to the position. He compiled 95 receiving yards in Week 4 against Cincinnati to lead the Jaguars. Strange had recorded just 72 yards over the preceding three games combined, and he's likely to return to a reduced role in Week 5 against an Eagles defense that's holding TEs to 39 yards per game and has yet to allow a TD to the position. While Strange can be worth streaming in the right matchups, Week 5 isn't one of those.

player.seasonOutlook: Strange played well in his first season as Jacksonville's clear No. 1 tight end, but it simply didn't lead to much fantasy success. The 2023 second-round pick handled a solid 16% target share during the 12 games he was healthy, but that was only enough to lead to 9.8 fantasy PPG (18th among tight ends). Strange simply hasn't been utilized much near the goal line, as he's yet to clear three touchdowns or four end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old is a reliable target for QB Trevor Lawrence, but with the team so well-stocked at wide receiver, consistent fantasy production is a long shot. Consider Strange a low-ceiling TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kaelon Black is coming off an impressive NFL debut as San Francisco heads into a Week 2 matchup versus the Dolphins. Black surprisingly got more carries than Christian McCaffrey in a season-opening win over the Rams, logging 14 carries for 65 yards to McCaffrey's 10 carries for 68 yards. While there's no chance of Black usurping a healthy McCaffrey in the pecking order anytime soon, the Week 1 usage suggests Black could take on a significant role in San Francisco's offense if the team looks to lighten McCaffrey's workload. Both backs could be in for a good day against Miami, who allowed Las Vegas running backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington to combine for 143 rushing yards, 45 receiving yards and two touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kaelon Black enters a Week 3 tilt against Arizona having established himself as San Francisco's clear No. 2 back. While Black has caught only one pass (on one target) through two contests, he's carried the ball 21 times -- one more than starter Christian McCaffrey (20 carries) and well ahead of No. 3 RB Jordan James (four totes). Of course, McCaffrey is the unquestioned leader of the 49ers' backfield, but Black has at least carved out a significant role and put himself on the fantasy radar in his first NFL campaign. The Cardinals just gave up 144 total rushing yards to Seattle's Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson in a loss Sunday, so they could be vulnerable against San Francisco's ground game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kaelon Black has seen his involvement on offense dwindle in recent games as the 49ers prepare to face the Broncos in Week 4. After the rookie garnered a hefty 14 carries in Week 1, he's logged just 11 totes over the subsequent two weeks, including just four this past Sunday in a win over Arizona. Black was at least fairly efficient by gaining 17 yards on those carries, but with only one reception to date this season, he's not getting enough touches to make an impact in fantasy. Perhaps that will change against the Broncos, who are giving up 5.26 yards per carry to running backs, the second-worst mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kaelon Black should continue to back up 49ers star RB Christian McCaffrey in Week 5 against Seattle. Black surprisingly logged 14 carries in Week 1 against the Rams, but since then he's topped out at seven totes as McCaffrey has dominated touches out of the backfield. Black also has just one catch this season, so he hasn't been able to establish much fantasy value except as an insurance policy in case of a McCaffrey injury. It may be hard for Black to find success on what will likely be limited opportunities against Seattle, as the Seahawks are allowing a paltry 3.35 yards per carry to RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Black was selected by the 49ers in the third round of April's draft. It was a bit of a surprise selection after Black failed to clear 190 touches in four collegiate seasons prior to not landing an invite to the scouting combine. He did clear 1,000 rushing yards at Indiana in 2025, but remained a nonfactor as a receiver, totaling exactly four receptions in each of his two seasons with the Hoosiers. Black will open his career handling No. 2 duties behind Christian McCaffrey. He'll be worth an add if the 30-year-old McCaffrey misses time, but a lack of third-down ability may severely limit his fantasy output. Stash Black in dynasty formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are on the road in Week 2 to take on Houston. The Texans have the 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to TEs, and they are last in receiving yards allowed to the position after Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox combined for 137 yards last week. Gesicki led the Bengals in catches (5), targets (7), and receiving yards (78) in Week 1, to go along with one TD. He could be primed for another big performance in what may very well be another high-scoring affair.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 3. After leading Cincinnati in receptions, yards, and targets in the season opener, Gesicki failed to record a single target versus the Texans in Week 2. Some of that could be chalked up to game flow with the Bengals ahead for most of the game, but it's nonetheless worrisome. The Steelers rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (5.5) and are first in receptions allowed to TEs through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town in Week 4. He caught all three of his targets for 37 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Gesicki finished third in receiving yards while catching his second TD of the young season, just one week after failing to earn a target. Jacksonville's defense ranks fifth in fantasy points allowed (7.8) and second in receptions (8) to TEs, so he could be in for another quiet day.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals travel to take on the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He grabbed three of five targets for 40 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss. Gesicki now has two straight outings with a TD and recorded his third overall, and he could be in line for an uptick in opportunities in a favorable matchup versus a Miami defense that allows 18.6 fantasy points to TEs, which is tied for 28th. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (adductor), and Colbie Young (knee) are all questionable, potentially leaving Gesicki as one of Joe Burrow's primary receivers against a Dolphins unit that just gave up 13 receptions and 119 yards to T.J. Hockenson

player.seasonOutlook: There was an era when Gesicki was a viable starting option in fantasy, but that time has come and gone. Since posting back-to-back top-eight fantasy campaigns in 2020 and 2021, Gesicki has finished 23rd, 37th, 13th and 41st the past four seasons. The latter came during a 2025 campaign in which he was limited to 41 targets in 13 games. Gesicki is no more than a situational seam stretcher and not much of an option near the goal line (he has exactly two TDs and five end zone targets each of the past three seasons). The 30-year-old will be a risky streaming option even if Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins misses time.

After a miserable 2025 that saw them surrender the most yards while scoring the third-fewest fantasy points, the Commanders brought in a slew of offseason reinforcements, though it was more of a quantitative than qualitative process. There's no reason to trust this D/ST in Weeks 1 and 2, which are road matchups with the Eagles and Cowboys, but if the Commanders show midseason promise, bear in mind its most favorable matchups come during the season's second half.

outlooksByWeek.2: Adonai Mitchell will look to stretch the field for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Mitchell hauled in all three of his targets to open the year, finishing with 60 yards. Green Bay allowed a mere 7.7 yards per target in Week 1, but that was largely due to facing Carson Wentz for the bulk of the game. Their secondary remains vulnerable and will likely commit multiple bodies to Garrett Wilson, setting up Mitchell for a few plays downfield in single coverage. Mitchell seems likely to continue his low-volume, high-upside role in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Adonai Mitchell hopes for a continued elevated workload in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. After just three targets in a run-heavy Week 1, Mitchell logged an eye-opening 12 targets in Week 2, with the Jets throwing 41 times. Detroit's defense has been a fantasy bonanza for opposing offenses, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts. Assuming the Lions score plenty themselves, the Jets should throw heavily, giving Mitchell ample opportunities for a big play or two.
outlooksByWeek.4: Adonai Mitchell is questionable for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears after missing Week 3 due to a finger injury. Mitchell has been a valuable secondary option opposite Garrett Wilson in his first two games, garnering 15 targets and averaging 13.7 yards per catch. With minimal options behind him and running back Breece Hall (thigh) likely to miss Week 4, Mitchell could have a stable workload against a defense that's allowing 8.5 yards per target to opposing receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Adonai Mitchell needs to overcome a finger injury that has cost him the last two weeks if he's to help the Jets against the Browns in Week 5. Prior to injury, Mitchell was giving the Jets a field-stretching option, averaging 13.7 yards per catch on nine grabs. Targets will continue to be heavily funneled toward Garrett Wilson, but Mitchell will be in a favorable spot if cleared to play, as Cleveland has allowed six touchdowns to opposing receivers through four games. Sterling Shepard and Isaiah Williams would continue to register additional snaps should Mitchell miss his third straight game.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell is entering his first full campaign with the Jets, having been acquired in the Sauce Gardner trade during the 2025 season. After playing sparingly during his first 25 NFL games (all with the Colts), the 2024 second-round pick handled a hefty 24.4% target share in eight games with New York last season. The usage led to two fantasy outings with 17-plus points, but he was otherwise a nonfactor (4.0 PPG). Efficiency remains an issue, as Mitchell's 44% catch rate ranks last, and his 6.0 yards per target is fourth worst among 77 receivers with 100-plus targets since he entered the league. The vertical threat will compete with rookie Omar Cooper Jr. for No. 2 duties opposite a now-healthy Garrett Wilson in the Jets' Geno Smith-led offense. Mitchell, 23, is not worth much more than late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.3: Darren Waller could remain a valuable part of the Panthers' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Through two games, Waller appears to be the Panthers' top receiving option at tight end, leading the TE room in yards (66), receptions (five) and touchdowns (two). However, having only received five targets through two weeks, Waller is likely a touchdown-or-bust streaming option going forward. He's in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Browns defense that's given up just 10.5 PPR fantasy points per game to the position this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Darren Waller continues to emerge as a major part of the Panthers' passing attack ahead of the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Waller had his most productive outing of the 2026 campaign in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, catching five of eight targets for 51 yards. He's taken over as Carolina's top receiving option at TE and could continue receiving more opportunities if Jalen Coker (hamstring) or Xavier Legette (knee) remain sidelined for Week 4. Regardless, Waller is in for a phenomenal Week 4 matchup against a Detroit defense that's allowed a whopping six receiving touchdowns to tight ends in three games this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers hope to improve to 2-0 when they visit the Patriots in Week 2. He secured all five targets for 46 yards and Aaron Rodgers' lone passing TD, and finished second on the team in receiving yards while tying for first in receptions. Freiermuth led Pittsburgh's TEs in offensive snaps (49), but Darnell Washington was a close second with 43. He and the Steelers will try to scheme up a way to beat a New England defense that is tied for second in receiving yards allowed to the position (13).
outlooksByWeek.3: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers play host to the Bengals for an AFC North clash in Week 3. He paced the team's tight ends in snaps (46), receptions (4), yards (32) and targets (5) during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Freiermuth appears to have the upper hand over Darnell Washington (1-7-0) in the passing game, but his fantasy floor and ceiling are relatively low in an underwhelming Steelers offense. He'll have the added benefit of facing a Cincinnati defense that allows 18.5 fantasy points per game to TEs (27th) and just got torched for 12 receptions and 140 yards by Dalton Schultz.
outlooksByWeek.4: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 4 AFC North clash against the Browns. He caught two of four targets for 30 yards and rushed once for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Aaron Rodgers continues to spread the ball around, as six different Steelers receivers registered at least four targets, and four tied for the team lead in receptions with three. Freiermuth could be a sneaky play versus a Cleveland defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (14.9) to TEs and gave up eight receptions (on 12 targets) for 92 yards to the position in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town for a Week 5 home tilt. He played 75% of snaps on offense and caught three of five targets for 17 yards and his second touchdown of the season. Fellow tight end Darnell Washington (3-27-1) was slightly more productive while playing 70% of the offensive snaps during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. They're both listed as starting tight ends for the Steelers, and it looks like it'll be a toss-up between the two on any given week as long as they're healthy. Indianapolis allows 13.7 fantasy points per game to TEs, which ranks 17th.

player.seasonOutlook: Freiermuth's career trajectory has been quite the head-scratcher, but the bottom line is he is yet to emerge as a consistent fantasy starter. The 2021 second-round pick flirted with TE1 status in both 2022 (11th in fantasy PPG) and 2024 (14th) but saw a dramatic dip in usage in Pittsburgh's crowded tight end room in 2025. Freiermuth posted a career-low 10% target share and finished outside the top 20 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and end zone targets, and 30 tight ends bested his 6.7 fantasy PPG. The 27-year-old figures to play more in 2026 with Jonnu Smith gone and Mike McCarthy running the offense, but Pittsburgh is also better at wide receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard in the fold. Freiermuth has some sleeper appeal, but he's best valued as a back-end TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase McLaughlin will look to remain perfect in the Buccaneers' Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McLaughlin made all five of his kicks during last week's loss, including a 51-yard field goal. With the Browns defense allowing 34 total points and 10 kicking points in a Week 1 loss, McLaughlin is likely in for lots more scoring opportunities in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase McLaughlin could remain one of the top kickers in fantasy despite the Buccaneers' tough Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 2 loss to the Browns, as he's now converted on all six field-goal tries this season, including two from 50-plus yards. Despite McLaughlin being tied for the league-lead in field-goals made this season, he could struggle against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 6.5 kicking points per game thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 4 matchup against the Packers. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, converting on all four of his kicks, including a 54-yard field goal. He's now made all nine of his field-goal tries and all five point-after attempts through three weeks. If Baker Mayfield (thumb) were to miss the Week 4 contest, McLaughlin may have fewer scoring opportunities. However, he's still in for a relatively favorable matchup with the Packers allowing 7.0 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chase McLaughlin is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. McLaughlin didn't attempt a field goal in the Week 4 loss to the Packers but made both of his point-after attempts. On the season, he's converted on all nine of his field-goal tries, including three from beyond 50 yards. McLaughlin could get fewer kicking chances with Jalon Daniels starting at quarterback for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb), but the Cowboys remain a favorable matchup, allowing 8.5 kicking points per game this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isiah Pacheco will miss Week 2 as the Lions travel to Buffalo. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he recently underwent surgery. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle whatever RB2 duties are available behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isiah Pacheco will remain sidelined in Week 3 as the Lions take on the Jets. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he recently underwent surgery. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy as the season progresses. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle any RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isiah Pacheco will remain out in Week 4 as Detroit faces Carolina. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy as the season progresses. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle any RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs in the meantime.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isiah Pacheco will remain out in Week 5 when Detroit travels to Arizona. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

player.seasonOutlook: Pacheco signed with Detroit in the offseason after a four-year stint with the Chiefs. The 2022 seventh-round NFL draft pick opened his pro career with a bang, totaling 2,139 yards and 14 touchdowns on 432 touches during his first two seasons (31 games). Injuries and a big drop in efficiency have limited him to 952 yards and three TDs on 232 touches over the past two seasons (20 games) and ultimately led to his exit from Kansas City. The 27-year-old will now get a shot to replace David Montgomery as Detroit's change-of-pace back to Jahmyr Gibbs. Pacheco might hit for the occasional touchdown, but he won't have standalone fantasy value unless Gibbs misses time. Consider Pacheco a late-round insurance flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deshaun Watson and the Browns visit the Buccaneers for an interconference clash in Week 2. In his first regular-season game since Oct. 20, 2024, Watson completed 16 of 22 pass attempts for 205 yards with one TD and one INT while rushing six times for 38 yards. Although his debut was uninspiring, head coach Todd Monken said he will stick with the 31-year-old as the starting quarterback after seeing enough positive glimpses on film. Watson will face another difficult matchup against Tampa Bay's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.7) to QBs and therefore should remain on waiver wires.
outlooksByWeek.3: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the Panthers for their home opener in Week 3. He completed 24 of 30 pass attempts for 238 yards with two TDs and no INTs, while rushing seven times for 22 yards during Cleveland's surprising Week 2 win over the Buccaneers. Watson led the comeback victory with scoring strikes of 55 and 17 yards, and chemistry appears to be brewing between him and the Browns' young playmakers. He'll face a Carolina defense that held the Falcons to 129 yards passing and forced three INTs and two fumbles in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the division-rival Steelers on Thursday night in Week 4. He completed 16 of 30 pass attempts for 144 yards with two TDs and no INTs while adding 11 rushes for 45 yards during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Watson did a lot of damage with his legs, a growing trend as he's racked up 105 yards on 24 carries across three outings. The Browns' offense continues to surprise, but they'll have their hands full versus a Pittsburgh defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points allowed (16.9) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Deshaun Watson and the Browns take their surprising 3-1 record into a road battle against the Jets in Week 5. In Week 4's 27-24 victory, he threw for 268 yards (24-for-33) with one TD and one INT, while rushing seven times for 22 yards. Watson lost one of his two fumbles, but he was able to do enough to lead his team to a third straight win. He hit seven different receivers en route to his highest passing yardage total since 2023. Watson aims to keep improving in a tough matchup versus the Jets, who have the second-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (16.0) to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson will return to the field this season after a disastrous four years in Cleveland. A top-six fantasy QB (points per game) during each of his first four NFL seasons, Watson has appeared in a total of 19 games since joining the Browns, averaging a poor 13.1 fantasy points during the span. A torn Achilles suffered in Week 7 of 2024 (followed by tearing it again less than three months later) cost Watson all of 2025. Now 30 years old, with a young, unproven supporting cast and having not been a factor since 2020, Watson will open the season as Cleveland's starter, but he's a long shot to return to fantasy relevance. He should be considered only in superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the Patriots for a Week 2 road clash. He completed 24 of 40 pass attempts for 221 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing three times for minus-3 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 victory over the Falcons. The Steelers attempted 41 passes compared to just 21 rushing attempts, as Rodgers connected with seven different receivers on the day. They'll face a tougher test on the road against New England's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.3) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the division-rival Bengals in Week 3. He threw for 187 yards (23-for-39) with no touchdowns and one INT and lost one of his two fumbles during Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the Patriots. Cincinnati has been somewhat stingy against opposing QBs, allowing 20.2 fantasy points through two outings (15th) despite giving up 353 passing yards versus Houston in Week 2. The Bengals are the only defense without an interception to this point, but they're also the only team that has yet to surrender a passing TD.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He's coming off easily his best outing of the young campaign, throwing for 292 yards (19-for-34) with three TDs and one INT while rushing three times for 10 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. Rodgers spread the ball around to nine different receivers, finding Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek for his three scores. He'll face Cleveland's 16th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.9) per game to QBs as the Steelers look to improve to 3-1 in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.5: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the Colts for a Week 5 showdown. He threw for 299 yards (22-for-40) with three TDs and two INTs during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. That's two straight outings with three passing TDs and nearly 300 yards through the air, but the 42-year-old was sacked five times in addition to his two turnovers. Rodgers will look to clean up the mistakes against a Colts defense allowing 24.3 fantasy points per game to QBs (27th) and 261.3 passing yards (29th).

player.seasonOutlook: Rodgers re-signed with the Steelers and will return for his second season with the team. The 42-year-old is reuniting with his longtime head coach from Green Bay, Mike McCarthy. The duo will look to improve on a 2025 campaign in which Rodgers finished just outside the top 12 in passing yards and touchdowns while ranking 23rd among 28 qualified QBs in QBR. Even if Rodgers' efficiency improves, he remains a nonfactor as a rusher (he last cleared 107 yards in 2020) and hasn't been fantasy relevant since 2021 (25th, 18th and 25th in points per game in his past three full seasons). Even with a more pass-friendly playcaller and with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard added to the wide receiver room, Rodgers is no more than a low-ceiling QB2.

The Raiders have a lengthy track record of defensive struggles, finishing in the upper half of the league in fantasy points from the D/ST in only one of the past 15 seasons. Still, the team added LBs Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker and CB Taron Johnson during the offseason, and it does still have DE Maxx Crosby on board. There could be some streaming potential here in favorable Weeks 1 (MIA) and 3 (@NO) matchups.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Mayer led the Raiders in targets with seven in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, although he turned that volume into just six catches for 32 yards. That opportunity came as Brock Bowers was sidelined following minor knee surgery, and while the third-year star isn't expected to be out long, he has yet to be cleared for Week 2. If Mayer does get the start at tight end, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in points allowed to TEs last year, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Mayer hasn't made much of an impact as the Raiders' top tight end through the first two weeks of the season, catching nine of 11 targets for 55 yards without scoring a touchdown. That role has come while Brock Bowers was recovering from minor knee surgery at the end of training camp, but with Bowers expected to return in Week 3, Mayer will see even his modest volume collapse. If Bowers' 2026 debut does get delayed further, Mayer will still be facing a Saints defense that has yet to allow a TD to a tight end so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Mayer's stint as the Raiders' starting TE ended in Week 3 with the return of Brock Bowers, but he stayed involved in a win over the Saints, catching all three of his targets for 32 yards and his first touchdown of the season. A lack of options at wide receiver could mean Klint Kubiak will continue to lean on both his tight ends for offense, keeping Mayer relevant even with Bowers as the clear No. 1 target for Kirk Cousins. Mayer could make a splash again in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that's been the stingiest in the league against WRs so far, but which ranks just 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Mayer was busy in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, turning a season-high 10 targets into eight catches for 82 yards. The additional volume came after wide receiver Jalen Nailor left the game with a concussion, forcing Kirk Cousins to lean even more heavily on his tight end duo of Mayer and Brock Bowers to move the chains. Even with a healthy Bowers back in action the last two weeks, Mayer has delivered an 11-114-1 line on 13 targets. However, he'll struggle to maintain that pace in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayer enters his first contract year expected to resume his role as Las Vegas' oft-utilized No. 2 TE behind Brock Bowers. The 2023 second-round pick has yet to come close to playing a full season, nor has he emerged as a reliable fantasy option. Last season, he averaged 2.9 targets and 3.4 fantasy points in nine games with Bowers, compared to 6.0 targets and 10.9 PPG in the four games in which Bowers was sidelined. A short-range target (career 5.5 aDOT) with minimal goal line work (one career end zone target), Mayer is way off the fantasy radar. He should be added to rosters only if Bowers misses time.

Chris O'Leary takes the helm as Chargers defensive coordinator, a year after this unit finished 11th in fantasy points (119). With stars like Khalil Mack, Derwin James Jr. and Tuli Tuipulotu on the roster, the Chargers should again put forth solid defensive numbers, health willing. But the biggest advantage here is the team's first-two-weeks' schedule: The Chargers host the Cardinals and Raiders, two of the most favorable D/ST matchups. Just beware that things get far tougher from there (@BUF, @SEA, DEN, @KC the next four weeks).

Run defense was the Bills' undoing last season, as they allowed a league-worst 24 rushing scores and snapped a seven-year streak of placing among the position's top 10 in fantasy points scored. Jim Leonhard was brought in as defensive coordinator, switching from a 4-3 to 3-4 scheme, though the team's personnel remains light up front. Regard the Bills a D/ST streaming candidate, and one better to leave undrafted due to their rough early schedule (@HOU, DET, LAC, NE, @LAR).

outlooksByWeek.2: Emmett Johnson contributed in his NFL debut, gaining 24 yards on eight carries and catching both his targets for 44 yards in a season-opening win over the Broncos. Kansas City leaned heavily on its ground game, with Kenneth Walker having a career-best day on 26 touches. Johnson's volume may be repeatable if this proves to be the team's offensive formula in 2026 and they continue building big second-half leads. Johnson will look to take advantage of his opportunities in Week 2 against a Colts defense that was just steamrolled by Derrick Henry but ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emmett Johnson logged only four touches as Kenneth Walker's primary backup in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, as the fifth-round rookie continues to get his feet wet in the NFL. Johnson also saw a little work as a kickoff returner as the team looks to find ways to get the ball in his hands. As long as Walker is healthy, Johnson's workload will remain limited, but he's flashed some big-play potential in the early going with 64 receiving yards on just four catches. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emmett Johnson remains in a limited role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Through three games, the fifth-round rookie has only 20 touches-16 carries and four receptions-but has managed to turn that into 120 scrimmage yards. Coach Andy Reid has hinted that Johnson's workload will increase as the season wears on, but as yet there's been no actual sign of that happening. Johnson will be a dart throw, albeit one with big-play upside, in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson was selected by the Chiefs in the fifth round of April's draft. His career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is fourth best in this RB rookie class and his elusiveness helped him to 1,451 rushing yards (fourth in the nation and first in this class) last season. His lack of speed -- last among 10 RBs who ran the 40-yard dash (4.56) and speed score (93) at the combine -- and size limits him after initial contact (career 2.86 YAC), but he can help out in the passing game (92 collegiate receptions). Johnson and Brashard Smith are set to handle No. 2/3 duties behind Kenneth Walker III. Smith will be worth rostering only if Walker misses action.

A middling, matchups-driven D/ST last season, the Buccaneers saw much change among their linebacker corps during the offseason. Lavonte David retired, and the team drafted Rueben Bain Jr. 15th overall and signed Alex Anzalone and Christian Rozeboom. Take a wait-and-see approach to how the new personnel jells, especially since the Buccaneers get a tough opening matchup in a road game against the Bengals.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trey Smack will look to stay solid as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Smack converted all three of his field-goal attempts against the Vikings in Week 1, but he did go 1-for-2 on XPAs. Still, the perfect field-goal percentage outshines his one miss. Smack will face a Jets defense that allowed a bottom-five fantasy points (4.0) total to Titans kicker Joey Slye this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trey Smack will aim to stay perfect as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Smack went perfect in Week 2 against the Jets, nailing two PATs and two field-goal tries, including a game-winner. The rookie kicker has now gone a perfect five-for-five on field goals and made all but one of his four extra-point attempts. He'll take on an Atlanta team that's allowed 9.0 fantasy points per game to kickers on the year, a bottom-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trey Smack will have a favorable matchup as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Smack went 2-for-2 on extra-point tries in Week 3 against the Falcons, but he also had his sole field-goal attempt blocked. The rookie kicker will seek to get back on track versus a Bucs squad that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (12.3) to kickers this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trey Smack will look to be consistent for the Packers once again in Week 5 against the Bears. Smack nailed a 58-yard field goal and both of his extra-point tries against the Buccaneers in Week 4. The rookie kicker has now gone 6-for-7 on field-goal kicks this season, with three of them from 50-plus yards. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked top five against fantasy kickers this campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Wright's role in the Dolphins' offense is limited entering a Week 2 matchup against the 49ers. Despite being their No. 2 back, Wright played just 6% of their offensive snaps to De'Von Achane's 88%. With Miami likely falling behind early and being forced to pass, Wright is far more insurance for Achane managers than a viable fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Wright's role is limited in the Dolphins' backfield entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. He has logged just seven snaps through two games and is now dealing with a stinger issue that makes him uncertain to play. With no clear immediate path to touches, Wright is an insurance policy in a matchup against a defense allowing 4.0 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out last Sunday. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins falling behind often in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the better pass-catching option of the two. Facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 ypc and 11 catches to running backs to date however doesn't inspire confidence.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Wright hasn't emerged from the Dolphins' backfield ahead of a Week 5 tilt against the Bengals. After missing Week 3, Wright was thought to have an ascending role following De'Von Achane's season-ending knee injury but received only five carries in Week 4 while Ollie Gordon shined with 100 yards and a touchdown on nine carries. It doesn't appear Wright was limited by the foot issue that cost him a game, as he remained the team's primary kick returner. Facing a defense that's allowing 4.5 yards per carry should afford Wright additional running lanes, but the role uncertainty puts Wright in wait-and-see territory rather than as a viable flex option.

player.seasonOutlook: Wright will once again compete with second-year Ollie Gordon II for backup reps behind feature back De'Von Achane. Wright has barely cleared 70 touches during each of his first two NFL seasons, but he has shined at times, including a 24-107-1 rushing line in Week 14 last season. The 2024 fourth-round pick has been effective as a rusher, but hasn't been involved in the passing game (15 targets in 25 games). The 23-year-old would be worth adding only in the event of an Achane injury and even then, it's possible he would split (or be on the short end of a committee) with Gordon in a rebuilding offense that may not score very often.

Micah Parsons' health has a bearing on the performance of this defense; it was 13th in fantasy points across the 13 games before his ACL tear, but had a negative score in four games without him. Tuck that away before diving head first into the team's soft September schedule (@MIN, @NYJ, ATL the first three weeks), though those are matchups that make this defense well worth streaming consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns visit the Buccaneers in Week 2. They'll face the fourth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.1) to WRs. Jeudy brought in two of four targets for 26 yards in Cleveland's season-opening blowout loss, but he didn't see any looks in the second half. He tied rookie Denzel Boston for second in targets and third in receptions, while fellow rookie KC Concepcion led the way with four catches and five targets. As long as the Browns' QB play remains shaky, there's no reason to consider Jeudy in any fantasy formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3, whose defense allowed just 145 yards through the air in Week 2. He failed to corral his lone target during Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2, giving him a 2-26-0 receiving line on five targets through two games. Meanwhile, rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion combined for 123 yards and one TD while catching 11 of 13 targets, and they look to be the leaders in the WR room. It will be difficult to start any of them until the Browns' offense consistently proves it can sustain any fantasy-relevant players.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns play host to their division rival Steelers in Week 4. He did not record a target in Cleveland's 21-18 Week 3 victory after failing to catch his only target in Week 2's win. Jeudy now owns a 2-26-0 receiving line on five targets through three games, and it's clear he's fallen down the offensive pecking order behind rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion and TE Harold Fannin Jr. He should remain on waiver wires against Pittsburgh's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.0) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns travel to take on the Jets in Week 5. He hauled in all three of his targets for 36 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4, setting new season highs in receptions and yardage. Jeudy had a solid bounce-back effort after failing to record a target in Week 3, but he remains behind Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion, and Harold Fannin Jr. in the offensive pecking order. Jeudy belongs on fantasy benches against a Jets defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points allowed (28.5) per game to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeudy's up-and-down career continues, as he has now finished outside the top 50 receivers in fantasy PPG four times in six seasons and inside the top 25 twice in the last four years. Jeudy has handled a target share in the 19-23% range all six seasons, but he hasn't found the end zone very often (17 TDs in 91 games) and has struggled with drops (32). Horrific efficiency (48% catch rate, 5.7 YPT) was a big issue last season and led to a career-low 7.1 fantasy PPG. Life might not be much better in 2026 with Cleveland's quarterback situation still unsolved and a lot more target competition (rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston join Harold Fannin Jr.). On the other hand, Jeudy, 27, is still in his prime and it has only been one season since he ranked sixth in the league with 1,229 receiving yards. He has some bounce-back potential, but Jeudy is safest as a bench player.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kendre Miller could operate as the Saints' No. 2 running back if Alvin Kamara (knee) remains sidelined for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Miller was surprisingly involved in New Orleans' Week 1 gameplan, tying Travis Etienne for the most carries on the team while finding the end zone. Despite averaging only 3.3 yards per carry, Miller could have a similar role if Kamara remains out for Week 2. It's also a favorable matchup for running backs, as the Ravens defense allowed 5.2 yards per carry and two rushing touchdowns in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kendre Miller is expected to split carries with Alvin Kamara in the Saints' Week 4 matchup  against the Falcons, with Travis Etienne (hamstring) out. Miller tallied 19 yards on six touches during the Week 3 loss, playing behind both Alvin Kamara and Etienne. As Etienne deals with an ongoing hamstring injury, Miller is likely to split work on the ground with Kamara in the Week 4 contest, operating as one of the Saints' leading rushers. Despite this, Miller is in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed just 3.1 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kendre Miller is likely to remain one of the Saints' top rushers while Travis Etienne (hamstring) is out during the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Miller received the second-most carries (six) on New Orleans in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons but was largely ineffective, averaging just 1.5 yards per carry. Even if Miller continues splitting work with Alvin Kamara, he likely won't have much fantasy value, as the Saints' offense is averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game. Additionally, Miller is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's allowed just 307 rushing yards all season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tre' Harris had a quiet performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching three of six targets for 20 yards. The second-year wideout struggled along with the rest of the passing game under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, with the exception of Ladd McConkey, and he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter with a rib injury. The injury doesn't appear to be serious, but if McConkey misses time, Harris could see additional volume. In Week 2, the second-year wideout will face a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points allowed per game to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tre' Harris caught only one pass in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, but he made it count, connecting with a scrambling Justin Herbert for a 53-yard gain that set up a third-quarter touchdown. Harris has just a 4-73-0 line on nine targets through two games, but if he continues to show he can gain significant yards after the catch, he could prove to be a good fit for OC Mike McDaniel's scheme. The 2025 second-round pick will face a Bills secondary in Week 3 that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tre' Harris is coming off his best performance of the season in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills. With Ladd McConkey limited by a rib injury, Harris handled a season-high seven targets and turned them into a 6-76-0 line that led the team. A second-round pick in 2025, Harris' ability to put together a breakout year will be hampered by the dysfunctional offense around him, but he appears to be close to moving past Quentin Johnston into the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. Harris faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tre' Harris is still looking for his first touchdown of the season, but he's been Justin Herbert's most reliable option, topping 50 receiving yards in each of the Chargers' last three games. Harris has put together a 13-209-0 line on 21 targets over four weeks, and he could make a push for the top spot on the WR depth chart with Ladd McConkey now dealing with both rib and foot injuries and Quentin Johnston failing to do much with his opportunities. Harris will aim for his first trip to the end zone in 2026 in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.

player.seasonOutlook: Harris is a Year 2 breakout candidate after flashing in a limited role as a rookie. The 2025 second-round pick quietly played 49% of the Chargers' offensive snaps, but he spent a lot of that blocking and was limited to an 8% target share. Harris is likely to open the 2026 season behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, but with Keenan Allen gone, his competition for No. 3 duties is 2025 fifth-round pick KeAndre Lambert-Smith and rookie Brenen Thompson. A potential starter in new playcaller Mike McDaniel's offense, the 24-year-old Harris is an intriguing late-round sleeper.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cooper Kupp and the Seahawks travel to Arizona to take on the Cardinals in Week 2. Kupp caught two of three targets for 35 yards in a season-opening win against New England, though he would have had a bigger performance if not for a 24-yard touchdown grab that was nullified by a penalty. Of note, Drew Lock is expected to start behind center for Seattle, as Sam Darnold is dealing with a glute injury and is unlikely to suit up. The Cardinals aren't expected to field a top secondary this year, but they did a good job of holding Justin Herbert and the Chargers' offense in check in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cooper Kupp has so far had a quiet campaign heading into Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington. Kupp has logged just two receptions in each of the Seahawks' first two games, registering 55 yards across the four total catches. He ranks third on the team with five targets, trailing Jaxon Smith-Njigba (22) and Rashid Sheheed (nine). As those numbers suggest, Smith-Njigba is dominating looks again this season, so Kupp and Shaheed may be left to compete for scraps throughout the campaign. With that said, there may be lots of receptions to go around against the Commanders, who have given up 27 catches to wideouts through two weeks -- tied for third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cooper Kupp is coming off his biggest performance of the season as the Seahawks prepare to host the Chargers in Week 4. Kupp logged season-best marks with four catches, five targets and 46 receiving yards against Washington in Week 3, and he got into the end zone for the first time with a seven-yard TD reception. Also of note is that Kupp logged a 67% offensive snap share after being on the field for just 43% of Seattle's offensive snaps the previous week. Kupp will look to build upon the promising effort against the Chargers, who have yielded a 67.3% catch rate to wideouts so far this season, seventh-worst in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cooper Kupp will look to rebound from a quiet performance when Seattle faces San Francisco in Week 5. Against the Chargers this past Sunday, Kupp caught just one of two targets for 13 yards. It was his lowest offensive output of the season, though he's been pretty quiet overall with two or fewer receptions in three of four contests so far. The 49ers are yielding just 123.5 receiving yards per game to wideouts, seventh-fewest in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Kupp heads into his age-33 season positioned for situational targets in Seattle's run-first offense. The longtime Rams slot man appeared in 16 games for Seattle in 2025 -- his first season with the team -- and was limited to a career-low 16% target share. Kupp was a nonfactor in fantasy, clearing 12.0 fantasy points only once (16.0 in Week 2). The veteran remains a reliable short-range target, but his ceiling is very low with Jaxon Smith-Njigba soaking up a huge share of the targets and the likes of Rashid Shaheed and Tory Horton also in the mix. Kupp is an unexciting late-round pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Antonio Williams led the Commanders in receiving in Week 1 despite playing just 26 offensive snaps. Williams ended up with four catches for 64 yards and a touchdown in his NFL premiere. He had as many targets as Terry McLaurin. Williams should see the field with increasing frequency if he continues to perform this well. He has a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus a Dallas defense that was the worst in the NFL last season, and surrendered three passing scores in the season-opening loss to the Giants.
outlooksByWeek.3: Antonio Williams snagged all three of his targets for 24 yards in the 37-20 loss to the Cowboys last game. Williams has seven catches for 98 yards and a touchdown through hsi first two NFL contests. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Williams and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Antonio Williams finished third in targets for the Commanders last game. Williams caught just two balls on four looks, though, en route to only 15 yards receiving. Williams caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Antonio Williams had eight targets last game for Washington, which was second on the squad behind Stefon Diggs. Unfortunately, Williams could muster just three catches for 21 yards in the lackluster loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Williams, regardless of whether Terry McLaurin also suits up. McLaurin was sidelined with a hamstring issue. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams was selected by the Commanders in the third round of April's draft. He is an undersized slot receiver (75% slot in his collegiate career) who soaked up 208 catches (fourth most in this rookie class) during his four seasons (43 games) at Clemson. He was primarily a short-range option (8.0 aDOT), but he caught a healthy 75% of his targets and added value as a rusher (career 25-187-2 rushing), punt returner and even as a passer (143 yards and two TDs on four attempts). Williams is in an all-out battle with the likes of Dyami Brown, Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane and Treylon Burks for the No. 3 WR gig behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs. He's worth no more than a late pick in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Justice Hill and the Ravens are at home to battle the Saints in Week 2. Hill rushed six times for 18 yards and had one catch for 10 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 win. He's established himself as the clear No. 2 RB, as his 31 offensive snaps trailed slightly behind Derrick Henry's 37. Hill should continue to see opportunities as a change-of-pace back against a New Orleans defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (38.4) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justice Hill and the Ravens travel to face a Cowboys defense in Week 3 that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) allowed to running backs. He tallied two carries for six yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss to the Saints. As long as Derrick Henry, who accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, is healthy, Hill's action will be limited as the No. 2 RB. However, in a contest that is expected to be high-scoring, Hill could contribute as a receiver, but he's still a risky fantasy play outside of deeper leagues.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justice Hill and the Ravens are back home to host the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He was explosive with his five carries during Baltimore's thrilling Week 3 victory, racking up 33 yards and a 6.6 average. However, Derrick Henry handled 26 of the 31 total carries for running backs, and he remains in firm control of the Ravens' backfield. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs, and despite the possibility of Baltimore playing from ahead, Hill's involvement will continue to be limited.
outlooksByWeek.5: Justice Hill and the Ravens visit the Falcons for a Week 5 showdown. He rushed once for three yards and caught two of three targets for 22 yards during Baltimore's 24-18 victory in Week 4. Derrick Henry out-carried Hill 23-1, even with Lamar Jackson missing the entire second half with an ankle injury. It appears that regardless of who's under center, the Ravens' backfield belongs to Henry. Hill should remain on fantasy benches against an Atlanta defense allowing just 17.9 points per game to RBs, which ranks ninth.

player.seasonOutlook: Hill heads into his seventh NFL season positioned for a larger role following the offseason departure of Keaton Mitchell. Derrick Henry remains the team's lead rusher, but he plays only about half of the snaps, leaving plenty of opportunity for Hill, particularly in passing situations. We've seen Hill in that role recently, including a 2024 campaign in which he posted a 42-383-3 receiving line on 55 targets (11th most among backs). Of course, Hill isn't trusted with much rushing work (his career high in carries is 84), which is why he has never had a top-35 fantasy campaign in his career. The 28-year-old has a limited ceiling and would be on the flex radar in PPR formats only if Henry were to miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tank Bigsby managed just one carry for the Eagles in Week 1. Bigsby rushed once for three yards in the 24-22 win over the Commanders. Meanwhile, fellow backup Will Shipley garnered three total touches for 12 yards. Both rushers remain firmly behind Saquon Barkley on the depth chart, though could see extra run in Week 2 if the game gets out of hand versus the Titans.  Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown in Week 2 versus the Titans after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger injury. Saquon missed portions of the game due to the ailment, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Bigsby and Will Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tank Bigsby returned to his backup role last game for the Eagles. With Saquon Barkley recovered from his stinger, Bigsby did not receive a carry in the dismal loss to the Bears. Barring injury, Bigsby will get little run in Week 4 versus the Rams. Los Angeles is allowing 101.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just one rushing score through the first three games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tank Bigsby replaced an injured Saquon Barkley last game for the Eagles, only to suffer an injury of his own late in the contest. Bigsby rushed 14 times for 55 yards to lead the Eagles before exiting with a lower-body issue. His status is up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. If neither Bigsby nor Barkley can play, Will Shipley would be in line for an expanded role. However, Jacksonville has played the run extremely well thus far in 2026. The Jags are allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tote, which us second in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Bigsby was acquired by the Eagles early in the 2025 season and progressively worked his way up to primary backup duties, a role he's expected to play again in 2026. Granted, it's a small sample, but Bigsby has been extremely efficient over the last two seasons. Among 48 backs with 200-plus carries during the span, Bigsby ranks first in yards after contact per attempt (2.75) and eighth in yards per carry (4.86). In fact, Bigsby has led qualified RBs in YAC each of the last two seasons. On the other hand, he hasn't been used much as a receiver (20 career targets). With overworked Saquon Barkley entering his age-29 season, Bigsby certainly has some insurance appeal, even if he defers passing-down work to Will Shipley. Bigsby, 25, is worth consideration in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Calvin Ridley wasn't targeted in Tennessee's season opener and is off the fantasy radar completely heading into a Week 2 home game against the elite Eagles secondary. The veteran WR may be as low as fifth in the Titans' WR pecking order behind Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor, and Chimere Dike. Second-year QB Cam Ward has struggled to keep any of his pass catchers consistently fantasy-relevant, let alone depth options.
outlooksByWeek.3: Calvin Ridley has drawn just two targets through two games in Tennessee's underwhelming passing game. The Titans don't have a player with more than 80 receiving yards heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants, so Ridley's fantasy value is slim to none as a depth piece behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson. The Giants have struggled to defend WRs, but Ridley is unlikely to get enough passes thrown his way to capitalize on facing the banged-up Giants secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Calvin Ridley has just two catches through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore. The Ravens have allowed the second-most catches to WRs this season, but Ridley remains a fantasy non-factor as a depth piece in a Titans offense that has generated the third-fewest passing yards in the NFL. Ridley is firmly behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson on the depth chart, and the 31-year-old WR has also been outplayed by Elic Ayomanor.
outlooksByWeek.5: Calvin Ridley has just three catches for 48 yards on five targets through four games. He's barely contributing as the No. 4 WR in a Titans offense that's averaging just 13.8 points per game, which is the second-fewest in the NFL. Even in a Week 5 matchup against a Texans defense that has struggled to defend wide receivers, Ridley remains a non-factor in fantasy.

player.seasonOutlook: Ridley's second season in Tennessee did not go as planned, as the veteran receiver missed 10 full games and was limited to a career-low 17 receptions. He remained a featured target when healthy (seven-plus targets in his four full games), but that led to only one double-digit fantasy performance. The lost season comes after Ridley delivered consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, finishing both as a top-30 fantasy receiver. Ridley is now 31 years old and has added target competition with Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson in the mix. A Year 2 leap from Cam Ward could get Ridley back into the flex discussion, but it's more likely that he's headed for a reduced role. Ridley is worth no more than a middle-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Bass continues to be busy for the high-scoring Bills' offense as they enter a Week 2 matchup with the Lions. In Week 1, Bass made three extra points and three field goals, though none were 50-plus yards. Detroit's defense, particularly the secondary, was suspect a week ago, and the Bills should score plenty, making Bass appealing.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Bass will attempt to bounce back from his first miss of the season when the Bills host the Chargers in Week 3. Bass wasn't afforded a field goal try in Week 2, with Buffalo's offense finding the end zone with ease, but still provided a reasonable floor, hitting five of six extra points. The Bills' offensive efficiency could cap Bass' scoring potential, but historically, the highest-scoring kickers come from the highest-scoring teams.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Bass' opportunities have been limited ahead of a Week 4 matchup between the Bills and Patriots. Through three weeks, Bass has attempted only four field goals, though Buffalo's high-powered offense has generated 12 extra points. New England's defense remains stingy, allowing just 15 total points to opposing kickers, likely keeping Bass out of Week 4 consideration.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Bass remains a stable floor, low ceiling kicking option for the Bills as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. Bass has collected 14 extra points through four weeks as Buffalo routinely converts drives into touchdowns, but only six field goal attempts, where he's perfect, keeping his scoring capacity limited. The Rams' defense has been stingy to opposing kickers, so don't expect Week 5 to be Bass' breakout party.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Holani looks set as Seattle's No. 2 RB heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Cardinals. Holani somewhat surprisingly logged eight carries in a tight Week 1 win over the Patriots, recording only two fewer totes than rookie Jadarian Price. However, Price was much more efficient with 5.2 YPC to Holani's 3.6. Price could get a larger share of the workload against the Cardinals, who limited the Chargers to 81 rushing yards on 21 carries in a season-opening victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Holani may be asked to take on a bigger offensive role for Seattle in a Week 3 matchup against the Commanders. Jadarian Price suffered a shoulder injury late in a Week 2 win against Arizona, and if he isn't able to suit up versus Washington, Holani would figure to see more work, though Emanuel Wilson would presumably take over No. 1 RB duties. As it is, Holani has gotten involved on offense in each of Seattle's contests so far, combining to produce 42 yards on 12 carries and two yards on one reception. The Commanders have been decimated through the air this season, but they haven't surrendered a rushing touchdown so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Holani appears to be settled in as Seattle's No. 3 backfield option heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Chargers. Holani logged 10 yards on three carries against Washington in Week 3, but he had by far his best game of the season as a pass catcher, recording five receptions on five targets for 48 yards. Both Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson seem to be firmly ahead of Holani in the competition for carries, so work as a receiver will likely be the key to Holani being able to make an offensive impact. The Chargers haven't been hurt much by RBs as pass catchers, yielding just 4.37 yard per target to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Holani looks to be locked in as Seattle's No. 2 RB heading into a Week 5 clash against the 49ers. That role didn't yield much fruit for Holani in Week 4, however, as he recorded just 18 yards on seven carries and two yards on one reception. Meanwhile, Emanuel Wilson recorded 120 total yards and two TDs on 24 touches, so he looks to be in full control of the backfield for the time being. San Francisco has given up just two touchdowns (one rushing, one receiving) to running backs this season, so they aren't a great draw for a player like Holani who probably needs to get into the end zone to put up meaningful fantasy points.

player.seasonOutlook: Holani is on the 2026 fantasy radar with Kenneth Walker III no longer on the Seattle roster and Zach Charbonnet (ACL) in doubt for the early portion of the season. Holani will compete with rookie Jadrian Price and Emanuel Wilson for touches while Charbonnet is sidelined. The 2024 UDFA has 25 carries and three targets to his name through two NFL seasons. Price figures to get the first shot at lead back duties and, even if forced into a few starts in Seattle's run-friendly offense, Holani would be working in a committee and no more than a deep league flex.

outlooksByWeek.3: Darius Cooper caught the game-winning touchdown for the Eagles in Week 2. Cooper managed just two catches for 26 yards, though one of them gave the Eagles the lead for good with precious seconds left on the clock. Cooper also tied for third on the team in targets for the game. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.5: Darius Cooper scored twice last game for the Eagles. Cooper finished the contests with seven targets, parlaying those looks into three catches for 33 yards and the pair of scores. If Devonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and/or Saquon Barkley are sidelined in Week 5 versus the Jags, Cooper could see an uptick in usage again.  Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Penix (knee) is expected to operate as Atlanta's starting quarterback if available for the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed 59 points to the Bears in Week 1. Penix has appeared in just 14 games during his two NFL seasons, throwing for 2,757 yards, 12 touchdowns and six interceptions. While healthy last season, Penix lead the Falcons to a 3-6 record while the offense averaged 20.6 points per game. He should be in for a very favorable matchup, with Carolina's defense giving up 40 fantasy points to Caleb Williams last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Penix is slated to make his 2026 debut during the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Atlanta has struggled offensively with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand as the team's quarterbacks over the last two weeks, scoring just 16 total points while Rush and Strand accounted for seven turnovers. However, Penix led the Falcons' offense to 20.6 points per game while throwing for 220.2 yards per game when healthy in 2025, suggesting improvement could be coming. Penix will be in for a tough matchup though, as Green Bay's defense has given up just 19.2 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Penix is expected to lead Atlanta's offense into the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. The 2024 first-round pick was impressive in his 2026 debut, throwing for 256 yards, one touchdown and one interception in a win against the Packers. Despite playing in the same division as New Orleans, Penix has never played a game against the Saints before. Following his Week 3 performance, the expectation is for Penix to elevate Atlanta's offense by getting the ball into the hands of Bijan Robinson and Drake London. Penix is in for a relatively favorable matchup as well, with the Saints' defense allowing 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Penix will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Penix has been great through two starts in 2026, throwing for 479 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. He's helped rejuvenate Atlanta's offense, as the team has scored a whopping 40 points per game since his return.
