Despite this, Penix is in for a tougher Week 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 18.8 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Penix is no longer guaranteed a starting job entering his third season. The 2024 first-round pick has appeared in 14 games and has 14 total touchdowns, a 21% off-target rate and a 60% completion percentage to show for it. Penix has done well to avoid turnovers (six career INTs), but he's a nonfactor with his legs (career 28-81-2 rushing) and failed to post a single fantasy outing better than 10th last season. Penix tore an ACL in Week 11, which further complicates his path to beating out newcomer Tua Tagovailoa for the team's Week 1 starting gig. The 26-year-old might eventually emerge into a fine NFL starter, but even if he does, his lack of rushing will limit his fantasy output. He's well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Willis looks to rebound from a shaky debut when the Dolphins again travel west to face the 49ers in Week 2. Willis was held without a touchdown pass in his first start for his new team, and while the rushing volume was lower than expected, he scampered for a touchdown. It's a challenging road spot against a defense that allowed just 168 yards passing and no scores in their opener, but game flow should remain positive for Willis to flirt with fantasy-worthy production. Miami will likely play from behind, necessitating throws, and dropbacks will continue to lead to rushing yards when pressured.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Willis figures to labor again in Week 3 when the Dolphins host the Chiefs. He has yet to top 220 yards or complete more than 15 passes through two games, and his rushing attempts haven't been as plentiful as anticipated. Any potential late production while playing from behind has also failed to manifest, and that game script figures to repeat in Week 3 against Kansas City, a defense that's allowed only 341 passing yards, two touchdown passes, and 12 rushing yards this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Willis will be under heavy pressure when the Dolphins face the Vikings in Week 4. Willis has just one touchdown pass through three weeks and has surprisingly topped 40 yards with his legs just once. Minnesota is the heaviest blitzing team in the league, so Willis will likely need his mobility often in Week 4. Without De'Von Achane (knee) and no emerging receivers, scrambling appears his only path to production against a defense that's allowing 7.0 yards per attempt while also allowing three touchdowns with four interceptions.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malik Willis will seek a breakthrough outing in Week 5 when the Dolphins face the Bengals. He has accounted for just two total touchdowns through four games and completed a mere nine passes for 85 yards in Week 4, both season-lows. An improved Cincinnati defense has allowed only four touchdown passes, but all of them have come over the last two weeks. With Miami's defense likely to give up points, Willis will at least have the opportunity to produce at a higher level than he's shown thus far.

player.seasonOutlook: Willis signed with Miami during the offseason and is set to start after two successful seasons backing up Jordan Love in Green Bay. Willis, a 2022 third-round pick, has very little experience (155 career pass attempts), but he was outstanding in limited work the past two seasons, completing 70 of 89 passes for 972 yards, six TDs and zero INTs (12.1 yards per attempt, 86% completion rate), while also adding major value with his legs (42-261-3) during the span. Willis played at least 80% of the snaps in three games with Green Bay and averaged 23.3 fantasy points in those outings. Willis' inexperience makes him risky and the Miami supporting cast is perhaps the worst in the NFL, but his dual-threat ability makes him a very fascinating late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chad Ryland enters Arizona's Week 2 matchup against Seattle as the NFL's co-leader in field-goal makes. Ryland converted four of five FG attempts in a Week 1 win against the Chargers, matching his 2025 season-high mark for field goals in a game. However, the veteran kicker had just 25 FG makes last year, so it may not be wise to expect such volume on a weekly basis. The Seahawks don't figure to provide Ryland with as many scoring opportunities, as they led the NFL with just 17.2 PPG allowed during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chad Ryland will hope for Arizona's offense to find more success in Week 3 against San Francisco. The Cardinals managed just seven points Sunday in a loss to Seattle, and Ryland's only scoring opportunity was a successful extra point on that score. He was much more active in Week 1, when he made four of five FG attempts and both PAT tries. The 49ers have given up an average of only 10.0 points through two games, so Ryland may see limited opportunities again in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chad Ryland heads into Arizona's Week 4 matchup versus the Giants having gotten off to a strong start to the campaign. Ryland made all three FG tries and all three point-after attempts this past Sunday against San Francisco, with his longest kick coming from 49 yards. Though he's yet to convert from 50-plus yards out this season, Ryland has been solid in going 7-for-8 on FG tries and 6-for-6 on PATs. However, his opportunities may be limited against the Giants, who have somewhat remarkably not given up a field-goal conversion through three contests this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chad Ryland showed off his leg in Week 4 and will look to do so again when the Cardinals square off against the Lions in Week 5. Though Ryland had only one field-goal attempt against the Giants this past Sunday, he impressed with a 60-yarder just before halftime. Ryland has now made eight of nine field-goal tries this season while nailing all nine of his point-after attempts. He could get plenty of opportunities against the Lions, who have given up a league-worst 31.8 points per game through four weeks.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens host the Saints for an interconference matchup in Week 2. The rookie third-round pick is doubtful to suit up with a fractured wrist sustained in the opener. Head coach Jesse Minter advised that Lane is seeking second and third medical opinions before establishing a timeline for his return. His health is something to monitor, but for now, his absence could make way for Devontez Walker (groin) and Elijah Sarratt (coach's decision).

player.seasonOutlook: Lane was selected by the Ravens in the third round of April's draft. Lane is a tall, perimeter receiver with the biggest hands in this rookie class. He produced solid 43-525-12 and 49-745-4 receiving lines during his final two seasons at USC. Lane was rarely used in the intermediate area and struggled to produce after the catch (career 3.7 RAC is second worst in this class), but he has the frame and skill set to allow him plenty of pro potential. He'll battle the likes of Devontez Walker and fellow rookie Elijah Surratt for work behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman in Baltimore's low-volume pass offense. Lane's primary value is as dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matt Gay was perfect in his Raiders debut, converting field goals from 30 and 47 yards and all three extra points in a season-opening win over the Dolphins. A rebuilding opponent certainly provided Gay with extra opportunities, but the Las Vegas offense could also be better than expected. New head coach Klint Kubiak and an improved quarterback situation, with Kirk Cousins steadying the ship until rookie Fernando Mendoza is ready, should help. The pending return of Brock Bowers will also help generate more scoring drives. Gay may not be able to squander any chances in Week 2 against a Chargers team that ranked ninth in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matt Gay has been busy to begin his Raiders' career, converting all three of his field-goal attempts and all six of his extra points through the first two games of the season. The outlook for the offense should improve once Brock Bowers is cleared for his 2026 debut, and while there's additional uncertainly on the horizon once first overall pick Fernando Mendoza is deemed ready to replace Kirk Cousins under center, Gay could actually benefit if the young QB struggles to get the ball into the end zone while he figures out NFL defenses. Gay will face a Saints team in Week 3 that's allowed an exact mirror to his production so far, with opposition kickers getting three FGs and six PATs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matt Gay has been both busy and perfect for the surprising 3-0 Raiders, connecting on all six of his field goal attempts and all eight of his PATs. The veteran kicker was also successful on his only attempt from 50-plus yards, as he looks to boot at least three long-range FGs for a sixth straight season. Gay has also benefited from a favorable early schedule, as all three of Las Vegas' games so far have been played indoors. The team will get a fourth straight game under a roof in a Week 4 home tilt against Kansas City, but Gay likely won't be able to afford to squander any opportunities versus an opponent that has given up just 16.7 points per game, tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matt Gay continues to benefit from the Raiders' surprisingly strong start to the season on offense with Kirk Cousins under center. In a Week 4 loss to Kansas City, Gay was a perfect 4-for-4 on FG tries while also converting his only PAT. The veteran has yet to miss an attempt in 2026, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 9-for-9 on extra points, putting him third in the NFL in kicker scoring behind the Vikings' Will Reichard and the Colts' Spencer Shrader. Gay likely won't be able to afford to start squandering opportunities in Week 5 against a Patriots team that's allowed 19.3 points per game so far, tied for sixth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeff Ulbrich's blitz-happy defense fueled 57 sacks, the league's second-best total, and a 13th best ranking in fantasy points. That approach could make this a streaming-worthy unit against weaker opposing quarterbacks, which could be the case with the Panthers (Weeks 2 and 18), Saints (4 and 17) and Browns (13). For those in deeper leagues, this could be an advantageous matchups-driven September D/ST if you wait until the end of the draft to fill the position.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mack Hollins will look to capitalize on an elevated role in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. Hollins caught four of his five targets to open the year, finishing with 51 yards, and could slide into A.J. Brown's (ankle) vacated outside role. Hollins and DeMario Douglas have the trust of Drake Maye, something that can't currently be said for Romeo Doubs, suggesting Hollins will play against a secondary that's without top corner Joey Porter Jr. Hollins' size makes him a capable red zone target, which generates upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mack Hollins will seek a bounce back performance in Week 3 when the Patriots face the Jaguars. After a solid four catch, 51-yard opener with A.J. Brown leaving early, Hollins notched only two targets in Week 2. New England's passing game is struggling with Drake Maye completing just 14 passes in Week 2. Until he begins to bounce back, trusting any of his pass catchers appears a risky proposition even against a defense that is allowing a generous 10.3 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mack Hollins will look to lead the Patriots' receiving corps in Week 4 against the Bills. Hollins gathered a season-high nine targets in Week 3, following just seven total in the team's first two games, as the Patriots continue to search for a top option without A.J. Brown (ankle) available. Drake Maye is struggling to move this offense, but Week 4 offers the potential to match the Bills' high-scoring offense. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers and an enticing 9.2 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mack Hollins' availability for Week 5 against the Raiders is in doubt due to a calf injury. Hollins has been a steady but unspectacular piece for the Patriots' receiving corps, going for 51 or more yards three times despite topping five targets just once with A.J. Brown sidelined by an ankle injury. Las Vegas can be vulnerable to opposing receivers, surrendering 70 or more yards four times. Efton Chism filled in after Hollins' early Week 4 exit and would likely do so again if Hollins does not suit up.

outlooksByWeek.2: Geno Smith may be called upon more often in Week 2 when the Jets face the Packers. He wasn't asked to do much last week as the club played with a rare lead for the majority of the game, relying on the run-something unlikely to repeat in Week 2. Green Bay's secondary is vulnerable, allowing three touchdowns to Carson Wentz to start the year. With more volume, Smith can ascend to the second tier of quarterbacks in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Geno Smith will look to be the next quarterback to take advantage of the Lions' secondary when the Jets head to Detroit in Week 3. Smith hasn't topped 250 yards through two games and has just one touchdown pass, but he is in a very favorable spot in Week 3, with Detroit having allowed three touchdown passes in each outing thus far. Smith threw 41 times in Week 2, and so long as the Lions are scoring, Smith will likely have high volume again, putting him in a position to have his best showing of the year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Geno Smith is facing an uphill battle if he hopes to match his Week 3 success when the Jets face the Bears in Week 4. Smith is coming off a sterling outing where he threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns, completing 84% of his passes against the Lions. While the Bears' secondary is vulnerable in individual matchups, their overall body of work has been stout. Chicago hasn't allowed more than 153 yards over the last two weeks, with no touchdowns and three interceptions. Despite Breece Hall's likely absence, the Bears are more suspect against the run, potentially setting Smith up for a game-management approach.
outlooksByWeek.5: Geno Smith hopes for more opportunities in the Jets' Week 5 game against a vulnerable Browns secondary. After completing 31 passes in Week 3, Smith went just 8-for-15 in Week 4 against the Bears. Despite the lack of volume, he has a 5:0 TD:INT ratio and a 7.7 yards-per-attempt average, his highest mark since playing just two games in 2016. Cleveland has allowed nine touchdown passes in four games and at least 291 yards in each of the last two weeks, putting Smith in a spot to exceed his season norms.

player.seasonOutlook: Smith was traded to the Jets following an unsuccessful one-year stint in Las Vegas. Smith, who began his career as a second-round pick with the Jets in 2013, is in line to start, though he's a long shot for consistent fantasy production. Smith peaked with a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game with Seattle in 2022, but he has finished no better than 16th over the past three seasons. He paced the NFL in both interceptions and sacks in 2025 after finishing third in both categories in 2024 and is no longer much of a factor with his legs. The 35-year-old might bring some stability to the fantasy outlook of the team's pass catchers, but we shouldn't expect much more than that. Consider Smith only in superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malachi Fields tied for third on the Giants in targets in Week 1. Fields caught two passes for 25 yards on four targets in his debut. Only Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely had more targets. The Giants are rather thin at wideout behind the aforementioned Nabers, and Fields is a huge target at 6-4, 225-lbs, so expect him to continue to be a decent contributor to the revamped offense. In Week 2, the G-Men will face a Rams defense that allowed 205 passing yards and three passing scores in a lackluster season-opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malachi Fields finished third in receptions and second in targets for the Giants last game. Despite seeing increased involvement, Fields caught just two passes for just 30 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Fields will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malachi Fields has two catches in each of his first three NFL games for the Giants.  Unfortunately, he has yet to find the end zone, and has not amassed more than 30 yards in any single contest.  Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Fields as well. Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malachi Fields scored his first NFL touchdown last game for the Giants. The rookie flashed his big-play ability, snagging a 40-yarder from quarterback Jameis Winston along with the 12-yard score. He finished with two catches for a career-best 52 yards and the touchdown. In Week 5, Fields and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Fields was selected by the Giants in the third round of April's draft. One of the biggest and strongest receivers in this rookie class, Fields figures to work as a perimeter, vertical target in the pros (career 13.3 aDOT during 49 collegiate games). Fields, who dropped just seven passes in college, handled a target share of, at least, 20% and air yard share of, at least, 30% during each of his final three collegiate seasons (two at Virginia, one at Notre Dame). Fields will battle Darnell Mooney and Darius Slayton for New York's No. 2 receiver gig behind Malik Nabers. The rookie is a fine late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: AJ Barner is coming off a quiet season opener as Seattle heads to Arizona in Week 2. Barner logged just two catches on two targets for 13 yards against the Patriots last Wednesday, though those two receptions were tied for second-most on the squad. Drew Lock played most of that game at QB for Seattle, and he's expected to start in Week 2 with Sam Darnold dealing with a glute injury. The Cardinals gave up seven catches for 90  yards to Chargers tight ends in a win Sunday, so Barner could be a key target for Lock.
outlooksByWeek.3: AJ Barner should again lead Seattle's TE corps in a Week 3 tilt versus Washington. Barner logged a healthy 56 of the Seahawks' 70 offensive snaps Sunday versus the Cardinals, but he finished with just one catch (on one target) for eight yards. Barner did boost his fantasy line considerably with a rushing touchdown, though his three catches for 21 yards through two weeks isn't going to turn many heads. Nonetheless, he could be a sneaky option for Week 3 against a Commanders defense that has already given up four receiving TDs to tight ends, tied for most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: AJ Barner will look to build upon a big Week 3 performance when Seattle hosts the Chargers in Week 4. Against the Commanders this past Sunday, Barner registered season-high marks with five catches, nine targets and 69 yards. That production was particularly notable after the third-year tight end compiled just three catches on three targets for 21 yards over the first two weeks of the campaign. Barner could find additional success against the Chargers, who rank in the bottom half of the league in receiving yards allowed to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: AJ Barner will look to amp up his production for Seattle in a Week 5 clash against the 49ers. Barner caught just one of three targets for 12 yards against the Chargers this past Sunday after posting a promising 5-69-0 receiving line the previous week. Barner logged nine targets in that Week 3 win over Washington, but he's drawn three or fewer targets in each of his other three contests. San Francisco has been tough against tight ends this season, giving up just 4.0 points per game to the position (fifth-best in the NFL).

player.seasonOutlook: Barner was a solid contributor for the Seattle offense last season. The 2024 fourth-round pick worked his way to the top of the depth chart, and although his overall volume was limited (20th among TEs in targets and yards), he found the end zone seven times and finished 14th in fantasy points (21st in PPG). The 24-year-old is a serviceable, short-range target for Sam Darnold, but even with some rushing worked in, his role in Seattle's low-volume passing offense won't allow much upside. In fact, it's possible he loses some targets to second-year TE Elijah Arroyo this season. Barner is a fringe TE2, at best.

outlooksByWeek.2: Najee Harris was a healthy scratch in Week 1 for the Giants, but that could change quickly. While Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary look like the 1-2 duo out front, third-string running back Tyrone Tracy lost a fumble in the red zone that could have proven costly.  Tracy had a rough camp even before the gaffe, so his time on the Giants could be coming to an end. If Harris does suit up in Week 2, he will be facing a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season.  The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.4: Najee Harris turned back the clock in the 12-7 win for the Giants over the Titans. Harris rushed nine times for 52 yards, and may have seized the backup running back job away from both Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants should continue to rely heavily on the running game in Week 4 versus Arizona, though Cam Skattebo remains atop the depth chart. The Cardinals have been suspect against the run in 2026, allowing 127.7 yards per clash on the ground, which is 26th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Najee Harris has received nine carries in each of the last two games for the Giants. However, he is averaging just 4.0 yards per carry as teams dare the Giants to throw with backup quarterback Jameis Winston, and remains behind Cam Skattebo on the depth chart. In Week 5, the G-Men will face a rather stingy Washington run defense. The Commanders are allowing just 93.5 yards per tilt on the ground, which is sixth in the league. However, Washington did allow three rushing touchdowns last game versus the Colts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Elliott was perfect on all four of his kicks in Week 1 for the Eagles. Elliott connected on a 33-yard field goal as well as three extra points in the 24-22 win over the Commanders. In Week 2, Elliott will face a Titans squad that allowed a plethora of points last season. Tennessee gave up an average of 28.1 points per clash in 2025, which was 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Elliott nailed a 58-yard field goal in Philadelphia's last game. Elliott has not missed a kick through two games for the Eagles, connecting on two field goals and six PATs. In Week 3, the Eagles will face a Bears squad allowing 23 points per contest, which is in the middle of the pack thus far this NFL season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Elliott did not attempt a field goal last game for the Eagles, as the offense was stymied in the 27-7 loss to the Bears. Elliott did hit his lone extra point, though has now made just two field goals in three contests thus far this season. In Week 4, Philadelphia will face a Rams squad allowing 21 points per tilt, which is tied for 13th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jake Elliott still managed two field goals and two extra points last game for Philadelphia, despite massive struggles on offense for the Eagles. Elliott has just four field goals through four contests, as the Philadelphia offense has sputtered in part due to a bevy of injuries to skill players. With DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and potentially Saquon Barkley sidelined for Week 5 versus the Jags, points may be at a premium. The Jags have also been extremely stingy in terms of points allowed this season. Jacksonville is giving up only 13.3 points per tilt, which is second in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to face the Texans for a Week 2 tilt. He was highly efficient with his touches in the season-opening win, tallying five carries for 20 yards while catching all three targets for 30 yards. Perine was the only other running back to record a carry, so his status as the No. 2 RB is not in question. Houston's defense is tied for third in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to RBs, but it surrendered 409 total yards of offense in their Week 1 loss to the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to take on the division-rival Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with an illness that forced him to miss two days of practice, he was active in Week 2 and recorded two carries for six yards and caught his lone target for 16 yards during Cincinnati's win over the Texans. With backfield mate Chase Brown handling 23 total touches, Perine's limited involvement on offense makes him a solid fantasy insurance policy, but nothing more. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 28th in rushing yards (233) and 29th in receiving yards allowed (97) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Samaje Perine and the Bengals play host to the Jaguars in Week 4. He rushed three times for nine yards and caught one of three targets for five yards during Cincinnati's 30-27 Week 3 loss. Lead back Chase Brown handled 13 carries, so Perine is firmly established as the No. 2 option and primary passing-down option out of the backfield. Jacksonville's defense ranks seventh in fantasy points allowed (17.2) to RBs, and it has surrendered just one rushing TD to the position through three contests.
outlooksByWeek.5: Samaje Perine and the Bengals are on the road to take on the Dolphins in Week 5. He tallied three carries for seven yards and failed to bring in his only target during Cincinnati's Week 4 defeat. Perine's offensive snaps and involvement continue to fluctuate as the clear back behind Chase Brown, even despite his team playing from behind more recently. Miami's defense ranks last in fantasy points (29.7) allowed to RBs, but Perine should remain on fantasy benches.

player.seasonOutlook: Perine is expected to resume his role as Chase Brown's primary backup in Cincinnati. The veteran back played 31% of the Bengals' snaps last season, totaling 84 carries and 21 targets. He cleared 400 total yards for the fifth consecutive season, though he has yet to reach 200 touches in a single season in his career, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. The 30-year-old has reached double-digit fantasy points three times over the last two seasons and would require a Brown injury in order to flirt with flex appeal. He can be left on waivers.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kayshon Boutte was held to one catch in his Texans debut, so he doesn't profile as a viable fantasy option for Week 2 against the Bengals. Boutte may still be learning the playbook after being acquired in an Aug. 24 trade from New England, and facing a tough Buffalo secondary didn't help things in Week 1, but he will need to demonstrate greater involvement in the game plan to warrant lineup consideration outside the deepest of formats. Cincinnati's secondary played well in Week 1, as no Buccaneers WR exceeded 63 yards against them.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kayshon Boutte had three catches in his second game with the Texans in Week 2 after going without a catch in his team debut. He's probably the best downfield option in the absence of Nico Collins (hamstring), who looks likely to sit out again in Week 3 against the Colts after missing the Week 2 loss to Cincinnati. The Colts have talent in their secondary, led by CB Sauce Gardner, but they are vulnerable to big plays through the air since they often leave their cornerbacks in one-on-one coverage with receivers. Indianapolis has allowed the most points and yards in the NFL this season, so Boutte has starter-level upside in deep leagues for Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kayshon Boutte has 79 yards on nine targets through three games with the Texans heading into a Week 4 home game against the vulnerable Dallas secondary. Boutte's 8.8 yards per target (YPT) trails only Jaylin Noel's 11.2 YPT among Houston's wideouts, while Xavier Hutchinson (21 targets; 5.7 YPT) and Jared Wayne (12 targets; 5.4 YPT) haven't done much with their chances. The Texans traded for Boutte in late August, so it's possible he's being brought along slowly and could start to see his role increase, especially if Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game in Week 4. Until Boutte starts getting more opportunities, the former Patriots WR will be difficult to trust in any format.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kayshon Boutte is averaging 29 receiving yards per game and has yet to score this season for the Texans. The former Patriots wide receiver hasn't shown enough with his new team to warrant lineup consideration in most fantasy formats in Week 5 against a Titans defense that has allowed three TDs to WRs through four games. Three other Texans wideouts have more yards than Boutte this season, as does TE Dalton Schultz.

player.seasonOutlook: Boutte was traded to the Texans in August. Reportedly a cut/trade candidate throughout most of the 2025 offseason, Boutte went on to lead the AFC champion Patriots' wide receiver room in routes and touchdowns while playing 67% of the offensive snaps when active. Despite the generous usage in a good offense, Boutte wasn't a reliable fantasy option, averaging 8.9 fantasy PPG. After seeing a career-high nine targets in Week 1, Boutte didn't clear five in a game the rest of the regular season. The 2023 sixth-round pick has finished in the range of 500-600 yards each of the last two seasons and has yet to produce a top-50 fantasy campaign. Now with Houston, Boutte will compete with Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel for Houston's No. 2 receiver role behind Nico Collins. Even if he wins that job, he doesn't figure to see enough work to find his way into the weekly flex discussion.

The Giants' linebacker corps is their D/ST strength, and it's possible this could be a sneaky-good source of sacks. Nevertheless, it's almost impossible to make a case to draft them, being that they face the Cowboys and Rams to open 2026. Should the Giants impress in those games, however, they could be a prime pickup for a soft Weeks 3-6 portion of their schedule (TEN, ARI, @WSH, NO).

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Brooks will remain in the backfield mix for Green Bay against the Jets in Week 2. While Brooks took an ancillary role to Marshawn Lloyd in Week 1, Brooks still finished the game with seven rushes for 29 yards to Lloyd's 13 for 37. Brooks is also an excellent pass blocker, so he'll still get time on the field even if it doesn't convert to rushing attempts. New York dominated Tennessee in the trenches in Week 1, but they should be a lot less daunting than a staunch Minnesota front.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Brooks should continue to stay involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Brooks was a non-factor on the ground against the Jets in Week 2 (four carries for 11 yards), but he did reel in his first catch of the season for 15 yards. The fourth-year running back should remain on the field for passing-situation plays moving forward, especially since he served that role last season even with Josh Jacobs on the field. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's been tough on RBs so far this season, allowing a top-10 16.3 PPR points per game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Brooks will remain an option in Green Bay's crowded backfield against the Buccaneers in Week 4. Brooks failed to register a carry and caught his sole target for four yards in a Week 3 loss to Atlanta, but he did log his third straight game with a 40-plus percent snap share on offense. The fourth-year running back's consistent usage on late downs as a pass catcher and a blocker makes him a valuable asset to the Packers, but not to fantasy managers at this point in the year. Tampa Bay has allowed the second-fewest rushing yards (165) but the sixth-highest receiving yards (165) to RBs on the year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Brooks will remain an option in Green Bay's crowded backfield if he's healthy in Week 5 against the Bears. Brooks rushed a solid four times for 30 yards and caught one ball for five yards in the first quarter of Week 4, but he then injured his ankle and did not record a stat after. The fourth-year running back will need to log some healthy practices this week if he hopes to play against the Packers' big rival. If he's able to suit up, Brooks will face a Bears defense that's allowed bottom-10 (4.73) yards per carry for RBs this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Ward threw for just 140 yards in Tennessee's 23-10 Week 1 loss to the Jets, bringing the 2025 first-overall pick's career average down to 184 passing yards per game. He's best avoided for fantasy purposes, even in multi-QB formats, for the Titans' Week 2 home game against the Eagles. Philadelphia's stingy pass defense limited Jayden Daniels to 164 passing yards and 4.8 yards per pass attempt in the Eagles' season-opening win over Washington.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Ward will be tough to trust outside of deeper multi-QB formats in Week 3, when the Titans face the Giants on the road. The 2025 first overall pick scored two short rushing TDs in Tennessee's surprisingly competitive Week 2 loss to the Eagles, matching his career total in that category heading into that game. Ward has just one touchdown pass this season and 16 touchdown passes through 19 NFL starts, of which he has won three. The Giants allowed two touchdown passes to Dak Prescott and four to reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, but those two veteran QBs are far more effective passers than Ward at this stage in their respective careers.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Ward has been arguably the worst starting QB in the NFL since entering the league as the Titans' first overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. In the first three games of his sophomore season, Ward hasn't thrown for more than 183 yards or recorded multiple touchdown passes in a game. Dynasty managers can continue to stash him on the bench for the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore in hopes of future improvements, but Ward's fantasy value in the present is negligible. The Ravens rank in the middle of the pack against the pass.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Ward hasn't thrown multiple touchdown passes in a game during the Titans' 0-4 start, and he's just 3-18 as a starter with 18 touchdown passes in 21 games. The 2025 first overall pick isn't an advisable fantasy option in Week 5 against the Texans, who have surprisingly surrendered the third-most passing yards in the league this season but still boast plenty of talent on defense and allowed the sixth-fewest passing yards in 2025. Dynasty managers looking for a silver lining with Ward can point to his season-high 222 passing yards in the Week 4 loss to Baltimore, 145 of which went to rookie fourth overall pick Carnell Tate.

player.seasonOutlook: Ward is eyeing a Year 2 leap following an underwhelming rookie campaign, albeit under tough circumstances. The 2025 No. 1 draft pick was plenty busy as a rookie (eighth in the league in dropbacks and pass attempts), but he struggled to 5.9 yards per attempt and took a league-high 55 sacks. Ward was rarely a factor with his legs (more than 12 yards three times) and produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 12th. The good news is that a tough rookie year isn't overly damning for a quarterback's career trajectory, and he'll be in a better spot in 2026 with new playcaller Brian Daboll and an improved supporting cast (Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson join a now-healthy Calvin Ridley). Ward will need to run more to become an elite fantasy option, but Year 2 is the breakout season for many quarterbacks, so he's well worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.3: Marcus Mariota will likely start for the Commanders in Week 3, as starter Jayden Daniels dislocated the same elbow that he previously injured last season. Mariota relieved Daniels in the second half in Week 2 versus the Cowboys, throwing for 111 yards and a touchdown. He will have his work cut out for him versus a devastating Seattle defense that is allowing just 8.5 points and 214 scrimmage yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt.
outlooksByWeek.4: Marcus Mariota led an improbable Washington victory over the defending Super Bowl champions last game. Mariota tossed three touchdowns in the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. Jayden Daniels is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4, though he is unlikely to play versus the Colts due to his dislocated elbow.  Whoever lines up under center will have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Colts pass defense. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Ejiro Evero coaxed a No. 15 positional finish in terms of fantasy points from this defense last season, and the defensive front has been fortified since with the additions of Devin Lloyd and Jaelen Phillips. There should be streaming potential with this D/ST, which could be worth the pickup for matchups in Weeks 3 (@CLE), 10 (@NO), 14 (NO) and 16 (@PIT).

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Nailor didn't make much of a splash in his Raiders debut, catching three of five targets for 27 yards in a season-opening win over the Dolphins. All three of the team's top wideouts, including Tre Tucker and Jack Bech, produced very similar numbers, with Bech catching the trio's only TD. The group figures to remain secondary pieces in the passing game as RB Ashton Jeanty and TE Brock Bowers, when healthy, figure to be the top weapons for Kirk Cousins and, eventually, Fernando Mendoza. Nailor isn't likely to break out in Week 2 against a Chargers' secondary that finished last season tied for eighth in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Nailor has had a quiet start to his Raiders' tenure, catching four of eight targets for 36 yards through two games without a touchdown. He hasn't been able to get on the same page as quarterback Kirk Cousins, even though the two were together in Minnesota for the first two years of Nailor's career, and the impending return of Brock Bowers will bump everyone else down a rung in the pecking order for looks. Nailor seems unlikely to break out in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Nailor has yet to earn much of a role as a pass catcher through his first three weeks as a Raider. While the fifth-year wide receiver does the kind of grunt work as a blocker that keeps him on the field, he's seen only 11 targets from Kirk Cousins and caught just five of them for 52 yards and zero touchdowns. With Brock Bowers making his season debut in Week 3 and immediately reclaiming his spot as the team's top target, Nailor's path to meaningful volume got even narrower. He faces a difficult task in Week 4 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jalen Nailor's tough start to his Raiders tenure continued in Week 4, as he failed to get a target before leaving the game early due to a concussion. The former Viking has a meager 5-52-0 line on just 11 targets through four weeks, and while his spot in the lineup seems secure when he's healthy due to his blocking ability, he hasn't established much chemistry with Kirk Cousins despite the fact that the duo played together in Minnesota. If Nailor does clear the concussion protocol in time, he'll be little more than a dart throw in Week 5, even against a Patriots secondary that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and which could be without top cornerback Christian Gonzalez.

player.seasonOutlook: Nailor signed with the Raiders and will battle the likes of Tre Tucker and second-year receivers Jack Bech and Dont'e Thornton Jr. for a starting gig in Las Vegas' new-look offense. Nailor was a rarely used commodity during his first four NFL seasons, all with the Vikings. The 2022 sixth-round pick totaled a 69-1,066-11 receiving line and never reached 30 catches or 450 yards in a single season. In fact, he's yet to clear six targets in a game. The 27-year-old very well could lock down a starting job in Las Vegas, but he's a long shot to make the big leap to consistent fantasy output in his fifth professional season. He's no more than a late-round wild card in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Nick Folk will look to bounce back from a tough performance in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. The 41-year-old went made just three of the five kicks he attempted in the Week 1 loss, missing field-goals from 54 and 45 yards. He could be in line to continue receiving scoring opportunities, with Atlanta's offense struggling to find the end zone last week. Additionally, Folk is in for a great matchup, with Carolina allowing 11 kicking points in a Week 1 loss to the Bears.
outlooksByWeek.3: Nick Folk's early-season struggled could continue in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers, who have allowed just 6.0 kicking points per game this season. Through two games in 2026, Folk has made just three of six field-goal tries, which is the worst mark in the NFL. He could benefit from the return of quarterback Michael Penix, however, who is expected to drive improvement after Atlanta's offense averaged just 8.0 points per game prior to his return.
outlooksByWeek.4: Nick Folk could have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Folk has struggled through three weeks this season, converting on just five of eight field-goal tries while making all four point-after attempts. He had his best game of the year in the Week 3 win over the Packers, making all five of his kicks (two field goals and three extra points). With Michael Penix back at the helm, Folk could see more scoring opportunities going forward. Additionally, Folk is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Saints defense that's allowed 7.7 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Nick Folk is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Since the return of Michael Penix in Week 3, Folk has converted all 12 of his kicks (three field goals and nine extra points), averaging 9.0 kicking points per game. With Atlanta's recent offensive success (40.0 points per game over the last two weeks) and Baltimore's defense having allowed 24.0 points and 7.5 kicking points per game, Folk is expected to have a favorable Week 5 matchup.

outlooksByWeek.3: Kaleb Johnson could continue to carve out a role as the Packers take on the Falcons in Week 3. Johnson saw a huge uptick in usage against the Jets in Week 2, logging eight carries for 32 yards. The second-year ball carrier was the most efficient of Green Bay's RBs, and he could continue to see an early-down role if MarShawn Lloyd remains inefficient. Still, Atlanta has allowed 127 rushing yards to running backs through two weeks, a top-10 mark, which could make Johnson's job tough even if he's the Packers' go-to on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kaleb Johnson will seek to earn more touches as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Johnson struggled to stay involved with Green Bay playing from behind in Week 3, logging just four carries for six yards and catching one of three passes for 10 yards. The former Steeler still saw his offensive snap share increase from 27 percent in Week 2 to 36 percent in Week 3, while Lloyd's share fell in the same stretch. This could open up more opportunities in the coming weeks, but not enough to start Johnson against a Bucs defense that's allowed the second-fewest rushing yards (165) to RBs on the year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kaleb Johnson will seek to stay involved as the Packers take on the Bears in Week 5. Johnson finished Week 4 against the Buccaneers with a solid eight carries for 42 yards, but he also lost a critical fumble in the fourth quarter. This makes it unclear what the backfield split will look like moving forward, not that there's been much of a clear breakdown so far. Chicago has ranked 26th in yards per carry allowed to RBs this season, which could carve a path for Johnson to stay productive if he can hold onto the ball.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson was traded to Green Bay in August after his rookie season in Pittsburgh didn't go as planned. Drafted in the third round as a potential Najee Harris replacement, Johnson quickly found himself buried behind Jaylen Warren and Kenneth Gainwell and never recovered, even losing his kick returner role after a costly Week 2 blunder. He ended his first campaign with 78 yards on 29 touches. The 23-year-old will enter his second season with a fresh start and very well could get some early-season run with Josh Jacobs facing a suspension. Johnson will compete for reps with unproven Marshawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks. Keep him stashed in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: Oronde Gadsden didn't have a big role in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, sitting third in snap share at tight end behind Charlie Kolar and David Njoku while catching both his targets for 32 yards. Njoku was the more productive receiver and Kolar by far the best blocker of the group, making it tough for Gadsden to find a niche in new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme despite his impressive numbers as a rookie. Gadsden faces an additional challenge in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that finished third in PPR points per game allowed to TEs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Oronde Gadsden hasn't logged much volume to begin the season, with just four targets through two games, but he's caught all four for 50 yards and scored his first touchdown of 2026 in the Chargers' loss last week to the Raiders. The second-year tight end's usage could increase significantly in the coming games. Both David Njoku and Charlie Kolar left the Week 2 loss to Las Vegas with injuries that are expected to land them on injured reserve, leaving Gadsden as the only healthy TE on the roster. He doesn't have the blocking skills of his veteran teammates, which could limit how much OC Mike McDaniel is willing to put him on the field, but Gadsden's workload will still increase almost by default unless the team is able to find immediate help from outside the organization. He'll face a Bills defense in Week 3 that ranks in the bottom 10 in catches and receiving yards allowed to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Oronde Gadsden didn't get a significant increase in his pass-catching assignments in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills, despite injuries to Charlie Kolar and David Njoku. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel prefers to have his tight ends block, which is not Gadsden's forte. While he saw a season-high 36 offensive snaps in Week 3, he only got three targets from Justin Herbert and failed to catch any of them. There still isn't any real competition for Gadsden on the roster at tight end, but fullback Alec Ingold ended up being the player who benefited most from the absences of Njoku and Kolar. Gadsden will try to prove to his new OC that he has more to offer in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Oronde Gadsden garnered his first significant target volume of the season in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, catching five of eight targets for 36 yards. The second-year tight end doesn't have the blocking chops offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel prefers, but with Charlie Kolar and David Njoku both injured and the team's wide receiver room also banged up, Gadsden is one of Justin Herbert's best remaining pass catchers. He'll try to build on this performance in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in receiving yards allowed to TEs through four weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Gadsden's rookie season was quite the roller coaster. The 2025 fifth-round pick didn't get much early run prior to exploding for 29.4 fantasy points in Week 7 and 18.7 points in Week 8. He went on to score one touchdown and average 6.2 fantasy PPG the rest of the season, never clearing 12.2 points in a single outing. Gadsden finished the season eighth or better at the position in end zone targets, aDOT, YPR, YPT and YPRR. The 23-year-old's second-half fall is concerning, and he now enters Year 2 set to compete for work with newcomer David Njoku and Charlie Kolar. It's still possible Gadsden emerges as a featured target in new playcaller Mike McDaniel's offense, but consistent fantasy output may be tough in an offense that figures to spread the ball around. Gadsden is only worth stashing in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jauan Jennings will aim to make more of his opportunities as the Vikings take on the Bears in Week 2. Jennings garnered just one target against the Packers in Week 1, and he was unable to convert it into a reception. The veteran was still on the field for almost half of the offensive plays, which keeps him as the WR3 moving forward. He'll look to get his first catch of the season against a Chicago defense that allowed the fourth-most PPR points to Panthers wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jauan Jennings will hopefully return to action as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jennings sat out in Week 2 due to personal reasons, so his practice availability this upcoming week should dictate whether he plays at the Bucs. The former 49ers wideout has yet to record a catch this season, but he played almost 50 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 1. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed 24.9 PPR points per game against wide receivers so far this season, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jauan Jennings will look to expand on his first catch of the year as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Jennings brought in one of two targets for one yard against the Buccaneers in Week 3, which is promising given that he was out due to personal reasons the previous week. The veteran should continue to operate as Minnesota's No. 3 option at wide receiver moving forward, but Justin Jefferson's injury does have a bearing on Jennings' usage. Miami has allowed a top-five 24.2 fantasy points per game to WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jauan Jennings remains a secondary option in the passing game ahead of Minnesota's Week 5 matchup at New Orleans. Jennings was projected to benefit from Justin Jefferson sitting out Week 4 with an ankle injury, but the veteran wideout logged just one catch for eight yards. He's now recorded two catches for nine yards in two weeks mostly without Jefferson, which especially doesn't bode well for his value when the star pass catcher returns to the field. He'll face a Saints defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Jennings signed with the Vikings in May. The 2020 seventh-round pick was a situational player during his first three pro campaigns in San Francisco prior to breaking out with a 77-975-6 receiving line and 27th-place finish in fantasy PPG in 2024. He dipped quite a bit statistically in 2025 and failed to produce a single top-10 fantasy week, but did score nine touchdowns (sixth among WRs) in a good Niners offense. The 29-year-old will now file in third on the Minnesota depth chart behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. He's headed for a big dip in targets and, especially with Kyler Murray under center, won't be a consistent fantasy option. He's barely worth late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylin Noel finished second on the Texans with 53 receiving yards in the season opener despite being targeted just twice. Noel will need to earn a larger role to gain fantasy relevance, but he has a chance to do so given Houston's lack of a clear No. 2 WR behind Nico Collins. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte combined for eight targets in Week 1 but recorded only 53 receiving yards between the two of them, matching Noel's yardage total. Noel can't be trusted as a starter heading into a Week 2 home game against the Bengals, but the 2025 third-round draft pick could be worth stashing, especially in deeper formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylin Noel could see extra opportunities in Week 3 if Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a second consecutive game against the Colts. Noel has just three catches this season, but two of them have exceeded 30 yards. The 2025 third-round pick's big-play ability makes him a viable deep-league option in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most points and yards in the NFL through two games. Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, and Jared Wayne are the other healthy options in Houston's WR room.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylin Noel is a deep-league dart throw for Week 4 against the Cowboys, especially if top Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) is sidelined for a third consecutive game. Noel is tied for fifth on the team with nine targets through three games, but he leads all of Houston's WRs with 11.2 yards per target. Given the Texans' lack of production from the position in Collins' absence, it would be sensible to give Noel more opportunities. Whether they materialize is another matter, and Noel's limited usage so far this season suggests he'll be tough to trust in Week 4, even against a Cowboys defense that's giving up 387 scrimmage yards per game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylin Noel turned three targets into 85 yards for the Texans in their Week 4 loss to Dallas, and the 2025 third-round pick continues to make the most of his opportunities. Heading into a Week 5 road game against the Titans, Noel has caught eight of 12 targets for 186 yards while leading the league with 23.3 yards per reception. Noel's big-play potential makes him worth a flier in deeper formats against a Titans secondary that has been prone to breakdowns, but he hasn't garnered consistent enough volume from C.J. Stroud to be started comfortably in any matchup.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Flournoy managed two catches for 22 yards on four targets in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Flournoy finished fourth on the team in targets for the game. The Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ryan Flournoy managed six targets last game for Dallas. Flournoy parlayed those looks into five catches for 23 yards. Flournoy was third in targets behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ryan Flournoy tied for the second on the Cowboys in targets last game. Flournoy saw eight balls thrown his way, though managed just two catches in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Flournoy also gained just 22 yards for the game; in fact, he has yet to gain more than 25 yards in any contest in 2026. In Week 4, Dallas faces a Houston defense that has been surprisingly subpar against the pass.  The Texans are allowing 238.7 passing yards per clash, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ryan Flournoy has been targeted at least four times in every game this season for the Cowboys. However, he has yet to cross 40 yards receiving in any contest. Versus the Texans, he had four catches but only for a season-high 37 yards. With a lot of mouths to feed like CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and even tight end Jake Ferguson, Flournoy's output may continue to be depressed. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league. Flournoy is still looking for his first score of the season.

player.seasonOutlook: Flournoy is an intriguing deep sleeper as the favorite for No. 3 wide receiver duties behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in Dallas. Flournoy flashed in 2025, putting up 14.2 fantasy PPG during the only five games in which his route participation was at least 60%. Flournoy did disappear quite a bit behind the heavily targeted Lamb and Pickens (three or fewer targets in seven of his final 10 games), so he's a long shot for standalone fantasy value even if he locks down the No. 3 gig. The 26-year-old should be added to rosters only if Lamb or Pickens are sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ray Davis remains largely uninvolved in the Bills' offense entering a Week 2 matchup with the Lions. He played more snaps on special teams (six) than on offense (five) in Week 1, and as long as James Cook remains healthy, Davis is an insurance policy more than a viable flex consideration. Davis' snaps would be further limited if RB Ty Johnson is able to suit up after missing Opening Week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ray Davis has limited involvement in Buffalo's offense entering Week 3 against the Chargers. Through two weeks, Davis has logged one carry and no targets as James Cook's primary backup, making his only contribution on kick returns. Facing a defense that's allowing just 2.98 yards per carry and with no clear path to an uptick in opportunities, Davis is an insurance policy for Cook managers only.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ray Davis hasn't recorded a carry in consecutive weeks or a reception all season as the Bills get set to face the Patriots in Week 4. Davis logged a total of 16 offensive snaps all season, with Ty Johnson's return as a passing-down back further hindering Davis's hope for work. He remains solely an insurance policy for James Cook against a defense allowing 4.2 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ray Davis has not been a part of the Bills' game plan entering a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. He has only two carries through four weeks, adding one catch while factoring in on kickoff returns. Seemingly losing snaps to Ty Johnson on passing downs in what was already a limited role, Davis's only fantasy appeal would be to James Cook managers in the event of an injury.

player.seasonOutlook: Davis is back as the primary insurance option behind Bills' feature back James Cook III. The 2024 fourth-round pick is one of the most valuable backups in fantasy, but flies a bit under the radar due to a very small game-day role when Cook and passing-down specialist Ty Johnson are both healthy. That's been the scenario most of the last two seasons, but we've seen Davis play more than half of Buffalo's snaps in three games. During those outings, Davis averaged 21.0 touches, 130.3 yards and 19.4 fantasy points per game. The 26-year-old has no standalone value, but he'll leap into the RB2 mix should Cook miss time, which makes him worth stashing on the end of your bench.

outlooksByWeek.4: Despite not recording a touch to date, Isaiah Davis could have meaningful touches in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears. Breece Hall (thigh) seems unlikely to play, elevating Braelon Allen to the lead back role with Davis as a secondary option. Allen hasn't shouldered a heavy load his entire career, having double-digit carries just three times, all during his rookie 2024 season. The Bears are allowing a generous 4.9 yards per carry, so even a handful of rushes for Davis could yield positive results.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Davis hasn't factored into the Jets' offensive plans ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Browns. Despite Breece Hall's (quad) Week 4 absence, Davis didn't receive a rushing opportunity and has no official offensive touches to date. Braelon Allen would again lead the Jets' backfield should Hall sit out again in Week 5.

outlooksByWeek.2: Wil Lutz's opportunities were minimal in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City, converting his only extra point and his sole field-goal attempt from 31 yards. The veteran kicker had been productive in his first three years with Denver, averaging just under 30 FGs and 38 extra points per season while going 12-for-18 on field-goal attempts of 50-plus yards. In Week 2, Lutz will take on a Jaguars team that ranked eighth in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wil Lutz has been perfect to begin the season for the Broncos, and in a Week 2 win over the Jaguars, he converted both his field-goal attempts and both his PATs. The veteran kicker has been consistent since following Sean Payton northwest from New Orleans, and kicking at altitude has allowed him to be reliable from long range, but the Denver offense doesn't provide him with enough opportunities to be among the elite at his position. Lutz will face a Rams team in Week 3 that just kept the Giants out of the end zone but which has allowed five FG attempts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Wil Lutz missed his first kick of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, hitting the left upright on a 43-yard field goal attempt but connecting on both his extra points. Game flow cost him opportunities, as Denver headed into halftime down 16-0 and attempted two-point conversions multiple times as part of their comeback. Lutz has converted three FGs and five extra points through three games, and his volume may not improve substantially until his offense develops some consistency. He'll take on a 49ers team in Week 4 that's allowed just 16.7 points a game, tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Wil Lutz continues to get little volume thanks to the struggles of the Broncos' offense. Through four games, the veteran kicker has attempted only five extra points, converting all, while going just 5-for-7 on FG attempts, with one of his misses coming from 58 yards out. Lutz is reliable, especially with most of his games coming either at altitude or indoors, but without more opportunities, he won't be able to make much of a contribution. He could get more chances in Week 5 against a Chargers team that has allowed 26.5 points per game, 24th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dominic Zvada connected on all four of his kicks in Week 1 for the Giants. Zvada made all four of his PATs during the 28-20 win for the G-Men over the Dallas Cowboys. He did not attempt a field goal for the game. In Week 2, Zvada and company will face a Rams squad that was surprisingly suspect in its season opener. Los Angeles allowed 27 points to the 49ers in a losing effort last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dominic Zvada accounted for the only points for the Giants last game. Zvada connected on both of his field goals in the 28-6 loss to the Rams. The injury to Jaxson Dart leaves Jameis Winston under center at quarterback, which could be an ugly development in terms of opportunities for points for Zvada. In Week 3, the Giants will face a Titans squad allowing 23.5 points per tilt, which is tied for 16th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dominic Zvada provided all of the offense last game for the New York Giants. Zvada connected on all four of his field goal attempts in the 12-7 triumph over the Titans. Zvada has yet to miss a field goal through three games, and could see additional opportunities in Week 4 versus Arizona. The Cardinals are allowing 27 points per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dominic Zvada continues to shine for the Giants as a rookie. Zvada made all three of his field goals, as well as an extra point, in the 36-24 win over the Cardinals. Two of Zvada's field goals were from 50-plus yards out. He is perfect to begin his NFL career, with five field goals already from 50-plus yards away. He could be primed for a big output in Week 5 versus a Commanders squad allowing 30.5 points per tilt, which is 31st in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jameis Winston will take the reins of the Giants offense in Week 3 versus the Titans. Jaxson Dart suffered a serious knee injury and may not return this year. Winston's performance in relief of Dart last game left much to be desired, as he completed just 11-of-27 passes for 111 yards and an interception. Against Tennessee, at least Winston will have a week to prepare and face a lower-tier defense. The Titans are giving up 233.5 passing yards per game in 2026, which is 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jameis Winston led the Giants to an ugly victory last game against the Titans. Winston was underwhelming to say the least, though, as he passed for under 120 yards for the second-straight outing. On a positive note, he did not throw an interception, and the Giants won the contest. However, the G-Men just traded for JJ McCarthy from the Vikings, which could put some pressure on Winston to perform. Nevertheless, Winston should remain the starter for now, and the Giants have another very winnable game in Week 4 versus the Cardinals. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jameis Winston tossed three touchdowns last game for the Giants. It was the full Jameis Winston experience, though, as the veteran also threw two interceptions. However, he finished 18-of-29 for 250 yards in the 36-24 win over the Cardinals. Miraculously, the G-Men currently sit in first place in the NFC East. In Week 5, Jameis and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass.  Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Winston is back with the Giants and with Russell Wilson out of the picture, he is expected to serve as the primary backup to Jaxson Dart in 2026. Winston hasn't been a full-time starter since 2019 and was limited to two starts last season. In typical Winston style, results varied, with 11.0 fantasy points against Green Bay in Week 11, followed by a 32.2-point showing against Detroit the very next week. The 32-year-old doesn't do much with his legs, but his boom/bust passing style makes him an occasional streaming option when the matchup is right. That's what he'll be, if called on for a spot start in place of Dart this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Bell hopes for additional volume in the Dolphins Week 2 matchup at San Francisco. Coming off an ACL tear in November, the rookie logged a 52.7% snap share in his NFL debut, ending with a 25-yard catch on two targets. Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas dominated the targets in Miami's limited passing game, as expected given their availability throughout training camp. The 49ers' secondary doesn't appear to be one where Bell can break out, allowing just 6.4 yards per target in Week 1. Bell is worth monitoring, but he's currently off the fantasy radar.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Bell will look for a breakout opportunity in Week 3 when the Dolphins host the Chiefs. He has drawn only three targets through two weeks, resulting in one catch and a declining snap share, playing just 40% of offensive plays last week. A potential absence from Caleb Douglas (ankle) could elevate Bell to a WR2 role in a struggling offense that often throws while playing from behind. Kansas City's pass defense has been stingy, but should Douglas sit, Bell would be an intriguing high-upside option if chasing points in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Bell will hope to build on his best game of his rookie season in Week 4 when the Dolphins face the Vikings. Bell posted seven targets in Week 3 after just three in the first two weeks, playing 72% of offensive snaps with Caleb Douglas (ankle) sidelined. Bell is the Dolphins' highest-ceiling option, but the passing game hasn't thrived under Malik Willis. Likely playing from behind, Bell could excel against a secondary that has misleading stats thanks to a Week 2 monsoon in Chicago that shut down the passing game, but Bell needs to turn potential into production before earning fantasy trust.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Bell is failing to gain traction in the Dolphins' limited passing attack ahead of a Week 5 tilt with the Bengals. Bell failed to record a catch on three targets in Week 4 in a game where Miami threw only 17 times, completing nine of them. Bell remains long on potential, but he's garnered three or fewer looks in three of Miami's first four games, and a breakout against a middling Bengals defense that hasn't allowed more than 63 yards to an opposing receiver seems unlikely.

player.seasonOutlook: Bell was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. The heaviest receiver in this rookie class at 222 pounds, Bell is a perimeter, possession target who increased his production in each of his four seasons at Louisville. That includes a 72-917-6 receiving line in 11 games last season, though he did tear his ACL in December. The injury could lead to a slow start to his NFL career, but considering he's joining a Miami offense devoid of playmakers, he also has a path to pacing the team in targets as a rookie. Bell could find his way to fantasy relevance if healthy and if Malik Willis plays well, but there are enough concerns that he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Hutchinson remains off the fantasy radar in most formats heading into Houston's Week 2 home game against the Bengals. He was third on the Texans with six targets in the season opener but finished with just three catches for 32 receiving yards. Hutchinson has topped 42 yards just twice through 50 career regular-season appearances.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Hutchinson drew nine targets in Nico Collins' (hamstring) absence in Week 2 but turned that into just three catches for 37 yards. Hutchinson figures to maintain a prominent role in Houston's passing game against the league-worst Colts defense in Week 3, especially if Collins remains sidelined. Whether Hutchinson can turn that significant usage into production is another matter, as he has usually failed to capitalize on such opportunities in the past, with only two career regular-season games of 42 or more receiving yards. Hutchinson is in the Week 3 deep-league flex conversation, but his lack of prior production is concerning.
outlooksByWeek.4: Xavier Hutchinson continues to do little with substantial volume, and that seems unlikely to change in Week 4, even with Houston hosting a weak Cowboys defense surrendering 27.3 points per game. Hutchinson has caught just nine of 21 targets this season and is averaging 40 receiving yards per game. Houston's lack of capable alternatives at WR figures to keep Hutchinson involved enough in Week 4 to earn deep-league flex consideration, especially if top wideout Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Xavier Hutchinson has exactly three catches in every game this season for the Texans and is averaging 42 receiving yards per game heading into a Week 5 road game against the Titans. He has drawn 11 targets in two games playing alongside Nico Collins and 15 targets during the two games Collins missed due to a hamstring injury. Collins should continue to work as C.J. Stroud's No. 1 option against Tennessee's beatable secondary, while the remainder of Houston's receiving corps is best left on the bench or waiver wire, Hutchinson included.

player.seasonOutlook: Mendoza was selected by the Raiders with the No. 1 overall pick in April's draft. The reigning Heisman Trophy winner and national champion, Mendoza is a big, pocket quarterback with elite accuracy (his career 7.1% off-target rate is easily the best in this rookie class) and a solid arm. Mendoza's 2025 campaign at Indiana included class-best marks in passing TDs (41) and QBR (90.3). He posted a 65-440-7 rushing line in 16 games last season and figures to add some value with his legs in the pros. Mendoza will get some run as a rookie, but his supporting cast isn't overly impressive and he will not start in Week 1 (Kirk Cousins will get the call), so there's not much sense in drafting him in most formats. He'll be worth a speculative add only when he's named Las Vegas' starter.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cade Otton will likely operate as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Otton caught just three of five targets for 26 yards in the Week 1 loss, but he was on the field for 56 of 57 offensive snaps, solidifying his role as Tampa Bay's top tight end. Additionally, Otton received the third-most targets on the Buccaneers, suggesting there's more production on the way. He's in for a favorable Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed 34 total points and 12.2 PPR fantasy points to TEs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cade Otton is expected to remain Tampa Bay's top tight end in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Through two weeks, Otton is tied for the most targets (11) and second-most receptions (eight) on the Buccaneers, which is a good sign for his outlook moving forward. He's currently on pace to finish with career highs in targets (93) and receptions (68), though is role could diminish once Jalen McMillan returns to full speed. Otton is in for a difficult matchup in Week 3, as Minnesota's defense has allowed just 9.9 PPR fantasy points per game to TEs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cade Otton is expected to remain a crucial part of Tampa Bay's offensive game plan in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Otton had his best performance of the season in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, catching three of six targets for 56 yards. Through three weeks, Otton is the only Buccaneers tight end to record a reception, which is a positive sign for his outlook going forward. Otton could struggle in Week 4 with Baker Mayfield (thumb) set to miss time, but the matchup remains favorable, as Green Bay has allowed 11.5 PPR points per game to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cade Otton will operate as the Buccaneers' top tight end in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Otton led Tampa Bay in receiving yards during the Week 4 loss to the Packers, hauling in four of six targets for 37 yards. He appears to have a connection with rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels and could be a solid spot-start in Week 5, especially while facing a Dallas defense that's given up 15.3 fantasy points per game and three receiving touchdowns to opposing tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Otton re-signed with Tampa Bay after spending his first four NFL seasons with the team. Since entering the league in 2022, Otton ranks first among all tight ends in snaps (3,530) and second in routes (1,838). That simply hasn't translated to much target volume (he is yet to clear 86 in a season) or goal-line work (11 TDs and 19 end zone targets in 63 games). In fact, Otton was the only player with 75-plus targets who didn't score multiple touchdowns last season. The 27-year-old has finished 25th or lower in fantasy PPG in three of four seasons and is a poor bet for his first top-10 finish in 2026. He's well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Higbee remains in a crowded Rams tight-end corps heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Giants. Though Higbee led Los Angeles TEs with two catches in a Week 1 loss to San Francisco, he logged only 12 offensive snaps -- fourth-most among the group. The Rams frequently use three-TE sets, so Higbee figures to be involved in some capacity each week, but he could have a hard time carving out consistent production if he remains at the bottom of the pecking order in terms of playing time. The Giants held a trio of Cowboys tight ends to five catches for 32 yards in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Higbee may be in line for an upgraded role for the Rams in Week 4 versus Philadelphia. After falling below a 30% offensive snap share each of the first two weeks and producing just two catches for 12 yards, Higbee exploded for an 8-62-1 receiving line on 11 targets and a 71% percent offensive snap share in Week 3 against Denver. That was partly due to fellow tight ends Terrance Ferguson (ankle) and Colby Parkinson (shoulder) getting hurt, and at least Ferguson (and possibly Parkinson) is expected to be sidelined for Week 4. However, the Eagles have been stingy versus tight ends so far, yielding only 89 receiving yards and no touchdowns to the position through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Higbee may have worked his way back up to the Rams' No. 1 tight-end role with a Week 5 matchup against Buffalo on tap. After logging just two catches over the first two weeks of the season, Higbee has tallied a 13-129-1 line over the past two weeks. He's led Los Angeles tight ends in offensive snaps in each of those contests, with injuries to Colby Parkinson (shoulder) and Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) contributing to the uptick in playing time. Buffalo has given up just one touchdown to tight ends so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Higbee re-signed with the Rams and will battle for work with the likes of Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson and rookie Max Klare. The 2016 fourth-round pick has a pair of top-10 fantasy campaigns in his career, but the last one came in 2022 and he's finished 24th or worse in three consecutive seasons. Injuries have been part of the issue (21 missed games over the last two seasons), but so has a lesser role and minimal goal-line work (seven touchdowns and four end zone targets over the last three years). Now 33 years old, Higbee is likely third in line for targets at his position on his own team and, thus, nowhere close to fantasy relevance.

outlooksByWeek.2: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 battle with the Patriots. The rookie should remain on waiver wires after playing just three of Pittsburgh's 67 offensive snaps in their season-opening win. Bernard is below DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, Jaylen Warren, Rico Dowdle, and Pat Freiermuth on the food chain, and it would take an absence or two from his teammates for him to see an uptick in playing time.
outlooksByWeek.3: Germie Bernard and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional showdown. With Michael Pittman (foot) on the sidelines last Sunday, the rookie stepped into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson. Bernard caught four of eight targets for 35 yards in the 20-3 loss, seemingly earning the trust of Aaron Rodgers rather quickly. He led the team in yardage, was second in targets, and tied for second in receptions. Bernard faces Cincinnati's 9th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (25.0) to WRs and should be considered a roster stash until we see this type of performance consistently.
outlooksByWeek.4: Germie Bernard and the Steelers travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He caught his only target for 14 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3.
