Sanders is back as a pass-catching tight end in Carolina, though he's unlikely to see a larger share of the target pie with veteran Darren Waller now in the mix. Sanders - a 2024 fourth-round pick - flashed as a rookie with a 33-342-1 receiving line while playing 55% of Carolina's offensive snaps and handling 9.1% of the targets across 16 games. He simply didn't progress in Year 2, posting a 29-190-1 line while playing 52% of the snaps and handling a 10% target share in 12 healthy games. Sanders has been an inefficient short-range target with little goal line activity thus far (four career end zone targets), placing the 23-year-old well off the fantasy radar.

Richardson enters his fourth NFL season as a backup to Daniel Jones. Last season, Richardson played just 14 snaps off the bench and missed most of the season with an eye injury. If ever called on to start, Richardson will be an interesting fantasy wild card. On one hand, the 2023 fourth-overall pick has a ton of upside; he ranked no lower than sixth among QBs in carries, rushing yards and rush TDs in 2024 despite only playing 10 full games, while also pacing the position in average depth of throw and yards per completion. That led to four 20-plus fantasy point games. On the other hand, Richardson's poor passing may lead to many duds. He had fewer than 15 fantasy points in his other six outings, threw 12 INTs on the season (fourth most) and his 48% completion percentage ranked last. In total, he averaged 15.8 fantasy PPG in the 10 games, which would've ranked 15th over the full season. Richardson's elite rushing ability and aggressive passing style are the only reason to keep him stashed in deep dynasty leagues.

outlooksByWeek.5: Mitchell Tinsley and the Bengals are on the road to square off against the Dolphins in Week 5. He caught three of seven targets for 49 yards in Cincinnati's Week 4 loss after the team signed him from Houston's practice squad leading up to the contest. Tinsley finished fourth in targets and tied for fourth in receptions while establishing chemistry with Joe Burrow in his debut. There's a real possibility he could operate as the No. 2 or 3 receiver for the Bengals with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (adductor), and Colbie Young (knee) all questionable versus Miami's third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Barion Brown will likely have minimal offensive impact in the Saints' Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Brown played just seven offensive snaps in his NFL debut, suggesting he's clearly behind fellow rookie Bryce Lance (62 snaps) in the Saints' receiving corps. With Tyler Shough attempting 56 passes in the Week 1 loss, it's tough to imagine a better scenario for Brown to make an impact as well. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup against a Ravens defense that's given up just 25.0 PPR fantasy points to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Barion Brown is expected to play a depth role in the Saints' receiving corps in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Brown has logged just nine offensive snaps through New Orleans' first two games, suggesting he's not a part of head coach Kellen Moore's offensive game plan. It appears as if the rookie's primary role is in the return game, as he's accumulated 34 punt-return yards and 128 kick-return yards already. Additionally, Brown is in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Raiders defense that's allowed just 6.8 yards per pass attempt thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Barion Brown (hamstring) is expected to play a depth role in the Saints' receiving corps if active for the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Brown was sidelined for the Week 3 loss but played a minimal offensive role prior to his absence, rushing once for three yards on nine offensive snaps. He's firmly behind Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance in New Orleans' WR room but will likely contribute on special teams when healthy. Despite this, Brown is in for a very favorable Week 4 matchup against a Falcons secondary that's given up 38.5 PPR fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown was selected by the Saints in the sixth round of April's draft. Brown is a thin, vertical receiver who handled a healthy 21% target share across 50 collegiate games at Kentucky and LSU. Brown struggled a bit with drops and efficiency, but made some noise as a rusher (32-228-2 across four seasons) and figures to make his biggest impact as a kick returner (65 kick returns for 1,910 yards and six TDs are all easily tops in this rookie class). With Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Jordyn Tyson (once healthy) cemented atop the depth chart, Brown is well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.3: Johnny Mundt caught two passes in Dallas Goedert's place last game for the Eagles, and would be the next man up at tight end if Goedert cannot suit up in Week 3. Goedert suffered a knee injury last game for Philadelphia and did not return, leaving his status in question for the clash with Chicago. Goedert is set to undergo testing to determine the nature and extent of the issue. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Johnny Mundt had a four-yard grab last game for the Eagles, as he is splitting tight end duties due to the injury to Dallas Goedert. Zach Ertz made his return to the Eagles, but it was not exactly triumphant. Signed during the week due to the injury to Goedert, Ertz managed just one catch for nine yards in the dismal 27-7 loss to the Bears.  Goedert's status remains very much in question for Week 4 versus the Rams. Even Goedert cannot suit up, the Rams have been rather stingy against the pass so far in 2026. Los Angeles is allowing just 171.3 passing yards per contest, which is fourth in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.5: Hunter Luepke continues to provide stellar blocking in the run game for the Cowboys. Luepke has not had a carry in either of the last two outings. He has just two rushes for eight yards on the season. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been stellar against the run in 2026. The Bucs are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. In addition, Tampa Bay has yielded just one rushing touchdown through four games.

Tez Johnson is expected to remain a depth piece in Tampa Bay's wide-receiver room in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Johnson has had an underwhelming start to his 2026 campaign, catching four of nine targets for 74 yards through four games. Additionally, the Buccaneers will likely continue relying on the running game more, as it favors rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels while Baker Mayfield (thumb) remains out. Despite this, Johnson should be in for a favorable matchup against a Cowboys defense that's allowed 8.3 yards per pass attempt this year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devontez Walker and the Ravens face the Saints and their 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (37.2) to WRs in Week 2. Walker, who has seven catches for 157 yards and four TDs across two seasons with Baltimore, sat out the Week 1 victory with a groin injury. Keep an eye on his status in practice leading up to their clash with New Orleans, as the Ravens are pretty banged up at receiver. Zay Flowers (hamstring) is considered day-to-day while rookie Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) is doubtful, meaning Walker could have a chance to make some noise if he suits up in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Devontez Walker and the Ravens travel to take on the Cowboys in Week 3. The third-year receiver hauled in one of two targets for 47 yards in Baltimore's Week 2 loss, good for third on the team in receiving yards. Rashod Bateman (7-88-1) filled in admirably for Zay Flowers, who sat out with a hamstring injury, but there's a high chance of the latter making his return to the field in Week 3. Walker's fantasy upside remains limited in a run-heavy offense, however, despite a potential shootout in Dallas.
outlooksByWeek.4: Devontez Walker and the Ravens host the Titans in Week 4 following their return from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. He failed to catch his only target during Baltimore's thrilling 34-31 win in Week 3, and he now has a 1-47-0 line on three targets across two outings. Tennessee's defense ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs, but Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Mark Andrews should continue earning the majority of looks from Lamar Jackson. Baltimore features one of the more run-heavy offenses with Jackson and Derrick Henry, ranking third in rush yards per game at 167.3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Devontez Walker and the Ravens are back on the road for the first time since the season opener to face the Falcons in Week 5. He caught one of two targets for 19 yards in Baltimore's Week 4 victory over Tennessee. Walker remains firmly behind Zay Flowers, Derrick Henry, Mark Andrews, and Rashod Bateman in the offensive pecking order. He should remain on waiver wires against a beatable Falcons secondary, allowing 38.4 fantasy points per game (T-27th) to WRs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahdae Walker will aim to stay involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Walker made a mark in Chicago's season-opener win over the Panthers with his limited opportunities, reeling in his one catch for a one-yard touchdown. The second-year wide receiver could continue to see success this season, especially if the Bears continue to score at such a high rate. He'll face a Minnesota defense that allowed two touchdowns to Packers WRs in Week 1.

outlooksByWeek.5: Ashton Dulin tied for the team lead with six targets in Week 4 against the Commanders as he returned from a two-game absence due to an ankle injury. Dulin has a chance to maintain a prominent role in the Colts' injury-riddled WR room against the Steelers in Week 5. Alec Pierce (ankle) is on IR, and Keenan Allen (groin) sat out against the Commanders, leaving Dulin competing with Laquon Treadwell and Deion Burks for playing time across from Josh Downs. The Steelers have been vulnerable in the secondary, especially after trading away starting CB Joey Porter, but Dulin's fantasy appeal is limited to deep leagues due to his lack of a track record, as he has just four TDs in 84 games.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Wright could continue to carve out a role for himself as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. There wasn't a lot of hype around Wright heading into the 2026 campaign, but the sixth-year tight end was on the field for nearly 50 percent of offensive snaps and reeled in his sole target for five yards. The veteran could be in store for more opportunities moving forward, and with the volatility of Sam LaPorta injury-wise, Wright is someone to keep on the radar. He'll face a Bills defense that ceded 14.4 PPR points to Texans tight ends this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Wright remains a depth option as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Wright remained on the field for a good number of snaps (26 percent) in Week 2, but the TE2 was unable to garner a target. The sixth-year tight end will need to run more routes before he can be trusted as anything more than a blocker. He'll also face a New York defense that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brock Wright will aim to stay involved as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Wright was in the game for a season-high 59 percent of offensive snaps in Week 3 against the Jets, and he logged two catches for seven yards in the outing. The sixth-year tight end remains a secondary TE receiving option behind Sam LaPorta moving forward, but Wright has shown an ability to register looks from veteran Jared Goff so far. The Panthers have ranked middle-of-the-pack against tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brock Wright will look to stay involved as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Wright stayed busy once again versus the Panthers in Week 4, reeling in one of two targets for eight yards. He's now recorded at least one catch in three of four games this season, staying involved even with Sam LaPorta getting most of the tight end targets. Wright will face an Arizona defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Bond and the Browns are in Tampa Bay to clash with the Buccaneers in Week 2. Although healthy and active for the season opener after clearing concussion protocol, Bond played just seven offensive snaps and didn't see any time on special teams. Cleveland's offense was not very good in its first appearance, and as long as questions remain at the quarterback position, there's no reason to trust any of their pass-catchers until proven otherwise.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Bond and the Browns welcome the Panthers to town for a Week 3 tilt. He caught his lone target for 10 yards during Cleveland's shocking victory over Tampa Bay in Week 2. It appears rookie receivers Denzel Boston (5-95-1) and KC Concepcion (6-28-0), along with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. (5-54-0), will be the focal point of the passing game, leaving Bond and Jerry Jeudy as the odd men out. Bond can be left on waiver wires in all formats versus a Panthers defense allowing 30.3 fantasy points (T-15th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Bond and the Browns host their division rival Steelers in Week 4. He was not targeted during Cleveland's 21-18 win in Week 3 after catching his only target for 10 yards in their Week 2 victory. Bond will continue to rotate with Jerry Jeudy behind rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, who combined for four catches and 50 yards on 13 targets. He should remain on waiver wires versus Pittsburgh's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.0) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Bond and the Browns battle the Jets on the road in Week 5. He caught his lone target for two yards during Cleveland's surprising 27-24 victory in Week 4. Despite the improved look on offense, Bond remains a very limited fantasy option behind rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, along with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. Bond should remain on benches against the Jets' ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.5) to WRs.

outlooksByWeek.4: Elijah Higgins will look to build off a strong performance this past Sunday as Arizona heads to New York to face the Giants in Week 4. After not drawing a target over his first two games this season, Higgins caught all three of his targets for 20 yards in Week 3 against San Francisco. Not surprisingly, however, his production was dwarfed by No. 1 tight end Trey McBride, who has caught at least eight passes in all three of the Cardinals' contests so far this season. Higgins' opportunities will logically be limited by McBride's massive role in the passing game moving forward, but there could be room for some success against the Giants, who have surrendered 18 receptions to tight ends this season, tied for ninth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Elijah Higgins will be fresh off his first touchdown of the season when Arizona faces Detroit in Week 5. Against the Giants this past Sunday, Higgins found paydirt from two yards out for his first TD of 2026. The veteran tight end isn't going to challenge star Trey McBride for snaps or targets, but Higgins has at least carved out a small role on offense with a 5-39-1 receiving line over his past two games. Though he doesn't get enough looks to be a reliable fantasy asset, Higgins does have a prime Week 5 matchup, as the Lions have given up a league-high six receiving touchdowns to tight ends this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colbie Young and the Bengals are in Houston for a Week 2 tilt against the Texans. The rookie fourth-round pick played just nine offensive snaps and did not record a target during Cincinnati's season-opening win. As long as Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Chase Brown, and Mike Gesicki are all healthy, Young's time on the field and opportunities will remain limited.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colbie Young and the Bengals travel to face the Steelers in Week 3. The rookie fourth-rounder caught his only target for seven yards during Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston, giving him his first career reception in his second game. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins accounted for 19 of Joe Burrow's 31 pass attempts, so Young remains firmly off the fantasy radar. In Week 3, he'll face a Steelers defense that ranks second, allowing just 15.5 fantasy points per game to WRs so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Colbie Young and the Bengals play host to the Jaguars in Week 4. Unfortunately, the rookie fourth-rounder has already been ruled out for that contest after suffering an injury in the first quarter of Cincinnati's Week 3 loss. Young caught his lone target for two yards before leaving the game. It sounds like the injury is not expected to be long-term, but the Bengals will take some time to evaluate the young receiver.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals travel to take on the 0-4 Dolphins in Week 5. He caught seven of nine targets for 82 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 Week 4 loss, setting new career highs across his receiving line, while returning six kickoffs for 161 yards and two punts for nine yards. Meyers finished second on the team in receiving yards and third in receptions and targets, and there's a decent chance he could earn a similar workload versus Miami's third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) are both questionable to play, along with fellow rookie Colbie Young (knee), and Andre Iosivas (thumb, IR) remains out for Week 5.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dyami Brown saw two targets in Week 1 for the Commanders. Unfortunately, he could not corral either target and went catchless in the opener. Meanwhile, rookie Antonio Williams looks to have cemented himself as the No. 3 wideout behind Scary Terry and Stefon Diggs with four catches for 64 yards and a touchdown to lead Washington. That being said, there could be plenty of ball to go around in Week 2 versus a Dallas defense that looked dreadful all of last season, as well as Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dyami Brown tied for second on the Commanders last game with six targets. That led to four catches for 21 yards in the 37-20 loss to Dallas. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Brown and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dyami Brown only had one target for the Commanders last game. He did not record a catch. Brown is vying with Treylon Burks and Jaylin Lane for scraps in an offense currently led by backup quarterback Marcus Mariota.  Still, in Week 4, Washington will face an Indianapolis defense that has been rather poor against the pass in 2026.  The Colts are allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bo Melton should remain a secondary option as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Melton was a solid returner in Week 1 against the Vikings, but he also recorded a pivotal 10-yard first-down catch in the matchup. This makes it evident that while small, the fourth-year playmaker's role on offense is not gone. He'll aim to stay involved against a Jets defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.5 PPR points per game against wide receivers in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bo Melton will aim to get involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Melton was unable to reel in his sole target in Week 2 against the Jets, but he did get an uptick in usage after Jayden Reed went down with an injury. Melton could be in line for more looks, especially if Reed misses a lot of time. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bo Melton could continue to see elevated usage as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Melton was on the field with Green Bay's offense for a season-high 32 percent of the time in Week 3 against the Falcons, but he failed to bring in his sole target. Still, the fourth-year utility man should continue to be deployed to some degree, especially since there's no return timeline for wide receiver Jayden Reed. Melton will face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-six 25.4 fantasy points per game to wide receivers in the first three games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bo Melton will aim to do more as the Packers take on Chicago in Week 5. Melton garnered his fourth target of the season against the Buccaneers in Week 4, but he was unable to reel it in. He's now commanded a target in every game this campaign, but converted just one for 10 yards. The Bears have also ranked top five against fantasy wide receivers this season, which could make it hard for Melton to do much once again.

outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Watkins heads into San Francisco's Week 4 matchup versus Denver with momentum on his side. Watkins played for the first time this season Sunday versus Arizona and caught both of his targets for 60 yards. That production came with No. 1 wideout Mike Evans (ribs/oblique) missing the entire second half of the contest, and Watkins' opportunities in Week 4 could logically depend upon Evans' ability to suit up. With that said, the Broncos could be a challenge for the 49ers' wideout corps as a whole given the 50.9% catch rate they've yielded to WRs so far (second-best in the NFL), though Rams star WR Davante Adams did just a 7-137-0 line on them in Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: Benson was selected by the Raiders in the sixth round of April's draft. An accomplished sprinter, the speedy Benson has big play written all over him, though he's a slightly older prospect and his collegiate production was limited by a lot of changes in scenery (two years of community college followed by 2023 at Alabama, 2024 at Florida State and 2025 at Oregon). Benson never cleared a 15% target share in a single season, peaking with a 43-719-6 receiving line in 2025. Benson is a longshot as a sixth rounder, but the Raiders' shaky wide receiver depth chart presents him with an opportunity to quickly earn a role. Still, he's no more than a deep sleeper.

Klare was selected by the Rams in the second round of April's draft. Klare is a receiving tight end who has experience playing in line and in the slot. He might not offer much as a blocker in the pros, but he showed his receiving ability at two different schools, posting a 51-685-4 line with Purdue in 2024 and a 43-448-2 line with Ohio State in 2025. Klare has the speed and athleticism to eventually emerge as a fantasy option, but hell begin his career in a crowded tight end room that also includes Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and 2025 second-round pick Terrance Ferguson. Klare is nowhere close to fantasy relevance at the moment.

outlooksByWeek.4: Braxton Berrios and Odell Beckham have been vying for the No. 4 wideout role on the Giants, though neither has a catch to date on the young season. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for both players. Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Braxton Berrios suffered a foot injury last game for the Giants. Primarily a returner, Berrios was targeted once in the passing game, though could not corral the target. Charlie Jones would likely continue to serve as the primary returner if Berrios misses Week 5 versus the Commanders. If Berrios can somehow suit up, he will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Olamide Zaccheaus is in for a very favorable Week 2 matchup when the Falcons take on the Panthers. Carolina is coming off one of the worst defensive performances in recent memory, allowing 59 points in a Week 1 loss to the Bears. Despite Zaccheaus playing just 18 offensive snaps and catching his lone target last week, he could find value in this incredible matchup. Zaccheaus' value could depend on which quarterback starts for Atlanta as well, with both Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) battling injuries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Olamide Zaccheaus is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving corps during the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Zaccheaus played 29 offensive snaps in the Week 2 loss to the Panthers -- which is 11 more than he did in Week 1. However, this didn't lead to an increase in production, as he caught just one of three targets for three yards. Zaccheaus could benefit from the return of quarterback Michael Penix in Week 3, but he'll likely have to find the end zone to be fantasy relevant. Additionally, he could struggle against a Packers defense that's given up just 5.4 yards per pass attempt this season, the fifth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Olamide Zaccheaus is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving corps in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Zaccheaus played just 34 percent of Atlanta's offensive snaps in the Week 3 win over the Packers, catching both of his targets for nine yards. He's made fairly little impact on the Falcons' offense this season, with Bijan Robinson and Drake London accounting for nearly all of the team's production. Zaccheaus is in for a tough Week 4 matchup as well, as the Saints' defense has given up just 9.2 yards per completion this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Olamide Zaccheaus is expected to continue playing a depth role in Atlanta's wide-receiver room in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Despite the Falcons' offensive success since the return of Michael Penix in Week 3, Zaccheaus has been less involved, catching just two of three targets for nine yards in two games. He remains firmly behind the likes of Bijan Robinson, Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Jahan Dotson as a pass-catching option and likely won't fantasy relevant without scoring a touchdown. Even so, Zaccheaus is in for a favorable Week 5 matchup against a Ravens secondary that's given up 8.4 yards per targets to wideouts this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tai Felton will look to get more chances in Minnesota's passing game against Chicago in Week 2. Felton garnered zero targets in a Week 1 win over the Packers, but he was on the field with the offense, which could contribute to some looks in the coming weeks. Veteran Carson Wentz played under center for most of the game, and Vikings receivers Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings both did not record a catch. Given that Wentz could serve as the quarterback again, Felton could fill a niche in the passing game behind Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson. The Bears defense also allowed the fourth-most PPR points to wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1, which could open up Minnesota's passing game even more.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tai Felton will aim to stay involved as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. After being on the field for five percent or fewer of offensive snaps in Weeks 1 and 2, Felton saw a major boost in Week 3 with 57 percent and garnered two targets. The second-year wide receiver did benefit from the departure of Justin Jefferson, but this uptick in usage could level out even with the return of the Vikings' star. Felton will seek to get his first catch of the year against a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against wide receivers so far.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tai Felton will seek to stay involved as Minnesota travels to play the Saints in Week 5. Felton benefited from star wideout Justin Jefferson being inactive in Week 4, logging his first catch of the season for 14 yards. The second-year pass catcher could be at a disadvantage this week, as Jefferson is aiming for a return. New Orleans has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Brazzell was selected by the Panthers in the third round of April's draft. He's expected to miss his rookie season due to a knee injury suffered in July. Brazzell is a tall, perimeter receiver with a big wingspan who will do most of his damage down field (career 14.2 aDOT at Tennessee) and doesn't offer much after the catch (3.6 RAC was worst in this rookie WR class). He has good speed (4.37 40-yard dash) and may settle in as a boom/bust low-volume, splash-play fantasy option. He'll battle for a starting role behind Tetairoa McMillan in 2027.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Brooks was a non-factor for Arizona in Week 1, but he'll look to make an impact versus Seattle in Week 2. Brooks logged just four offensive snaps in the season-opener versus the Chargers and didn't draw any targets. It didn't help his case for a larger role that newcomer Kendrick Bourne played well with eight catches on eight targets for 75 yards as the No. 3 wideout on the depth chart. All of Arizona's pass catchers face a tough challenge against a Seahawks squad that is expected to have one of the league's best defenses again in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Brooks has yet to get going this season heading into Arizona's Week 3 clash with San Francisco. Brooks hasn't yet drawn a target, but that's partly because he's logged just six offensive snaps through two weeks. Among Cardinals wideouts, only Michael Wilson, Marvin Harrison Jr. and Kendrick Bourne have recorded receptions so far, and it remains to be seen if the team will eventually look to get its other WRs involved. San Francisco has been strong against the pass through two weeks, ranking in the top 10 in most categories versus wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Klubnik was selected by the Jets in the fourth round of April's draft. Klubnik is an undersized, conservative quarterback who ranked last in this rookie class in aDOT (7.4), yards per completion (11.1), yards per attempt (7.1) and QB rating (136) during his collegiate tenure. He peaked with a 36-to-6 TD-to-INT showing in 2024, but fell to 16 TDs and six INTs in 2025. Klubnik does have a lot of experience (three years as a starter at Clemson) and could add value with his legs (totaled a 294-1,429-17 rushing line in his career), though he was extremely inefficient in the latter in 2025. Klubnik will handle No. 2 duties behind Geno Smith, but could handle some starts later in the year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brenen Thompson was on the field for just 10 offensive snaps in his NFL debut and failed to get a target in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals. The fourth-round speedster could still end up being useful in new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, but the whole unit is still adjusting. Top wideout Ladd McConkey left the game early with a rib injury, and if he misses additional time, it could open the door for Thompson to take on a bigger role, although he would still likely be behind Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris in the pecking order. In Week 2, Thompson will face a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points per game allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brenen Thompson began to work into the offense a little more in Week 2, notching his first three targets and catching one of them for 13 yards. That usage may have been due to Ladd McConkey nursing a rib injury, but Thompson's elite speed could earn a consistent spot in OC Mike McDaniel's quick-strike game plan if he shows he can get open against NFL defenders. Thompson will try to keep building chemistry with QB Justin Herbert in Week 3 against a Bills secondary that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brenen Thompson was unable to suit up in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills due to a quadriceps strain, denying him a chance to continue earning a larger role in the passing game. The fourth-round rookie has the speed offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel craves, but Thompson is behind Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris on the depth chart, and even once he's healthy he's unlikely to work his way into significant volume. If he's able to return in Week 4, Thompson will get a daunting matching against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brenen Thompson has missed the Chargers' last two games with a quadriceps strain, but if the rookie speedster is cleared to return soon, a big opportunity could be awaiting. Ladd McConkey is dealing with both rib and foot injuries and seems set to miss time, while Quentin Johnston has been disappointing once again. Thompson logged three targets in Week 2, his last healthy game, and he could get even higher volume if he returns in Week 5 to face a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.

player.seasonOutlook: Thompson was selected by the Chargers in the fourth round of April's draft. Thompson is an extremely small and very fast (4.26 40-yard dash) receiver who posted a rookie-class-high 18.5 YPR during his career and handled a massive 43% of Mississippi State's air yards last season. He didn't see much work prior to 2025, however, and figures to operate as a situational deep threat in the pros. He'll battle second-years Tre Harris and KeAndre Lamber-Smith for occasional looks behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston this season.

outlooksByWeek.5: Sam Roush will look to keep his catch streak alive as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Roush stayed relevant in Chicago's passing game against the Jets in Week 4, taking his sole target for eight yards. The rookie tight end has now recorded a catch in three straight games, posting a 3-33-0 receiving line on the year. He'll face a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against TEs so far.

player.seasonOutlook: Roush was selected by the Bears in the third round of April's draft. Roush is a huge, in-line blocking tight end. Though he did catch 40-plus passes each of his final two seasons at Stanford (including a healthy 22% target share in 2025), his overall receiving efficiency was underwhelming (6.6 YPT, 1.22 YPRR) and he totaled four TDs on 182 career targets. He's unlikely to see enough target volume in the pros to find his way to the fantasy radar and that's especially the case in Chicago, as he's buried behind Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Oliver will seek to stay involved in Minnesota's passing game at Chicago in Week 2. Oliver was an unlikely contributor against the Packers in Week 1, logging two catches for 22 yards and ranking third on the team in targets (four). With veteran Carson Wentz also very likely to serve under center once again, the seventh-year tight end could be in line for more targets. He'll face a Bears defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 11.5 PPR points to Panthers tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Oliver will aim to stay involved in Minnesota's passing game against Tampa Bay in Week 3. Oliver stayed active in a low-scoring Week 2 win against the Bears, reeling in his sole target for a 24-yard gain. The supplementary tight end has now amassed three catches for 46 yards off five targets in his first two outings. He'll take on a New York defense that's allowed a third-lowest 6.0 PPR points per game to TEs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Oliver was announced to be out for the season with a torn biceps ahead of Minnesota's Week 4 matchup against Miami. Oliver was looking to be a high-upside option in deeper leagues after three catches for 46 yards across two games and staying involved as a blocker. The veteran tight end will instead focus on rehabbing for the 2027 season, which should open up opportunities for T.J. Hockenson even more.

player.seasonOutlook: Delp was selected by the Saints in the third round of April's draft. Delp was busy during his final three seasons at Georgia (1,733 snaps in 42 games), but that didn't lead to much work in the passing game (no more than 24 catches, 284 yards or a 7% target share in a single season). Good speed and hands suggest there's some hope for him as a developmental piece, which is what he'll be in 2026 while playing a situational role behind Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant.

outlooksByWeek.5: Patrick Ricard has yet to see a carry this season for the Giants. The 300-lb fullback has served as the primary blocker for Cam Skattebo in this run-heavy offense. In Week 5, the G-Men will face a rather stingy Washington run defense. The Commanders are allowing just 93.5 yards per tilt on the ground, which is sixth in the league. However, Washington did allow three rushing touchdowns last game versus the Colts.

outlooksByWeek.2: LaJohntay Wester and the Ravens host the Saints in Week 2. The second-year receiver played 19 of 68 offensive snaps in the season-opening victory, hauling in both of his targets for 15 yards. He also worked on special teams, but with Zay Flowers (hamstring), Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist), and Devontez Walker (groin) all either questionable or doubtful to play in Week 2, more opportunities open up. New Orleans surrendered 206 yards and two TDs through the air in its Week 1 loss to Detroit.

outlooksByWeek.5: Marquez Valdes-Scantling had his first meaningful action of the season in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, playing 26 offensive snaps but failing to catch his only target. Ladd McConkey is battling both rib and foot injuries and seems set to miss time, while rookie Brenan Thompson has missed the last two weeks with a quadriceps strain. This could open the door for Valdes-Scantling to fill the No. 3 receiver role behind Quentin Johnson and Tre' Harris. If he does, the veteran deep threat might be able to hit a big play or two in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jacob Cowing stands to take on a bigger role in San Francisco's offense if Demarcus Robinson (ankle) can't suit up versus Arizona in Week 3. Cowing hasn't seen much opportunity on offense yet, playing just 27 offensive snaps without drawing a target through two games. However, Robinson seems likely to miss Week 3 due to his injury, and if that's the case Cowing would likely be called upon to step into a larger amount of work in the passing game. The Cardinals haven't been good against the pass this season and just allowed star Seattle WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba to rack up 155 receiving yards and three TDs in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacob Cowing could be in for a bigger role in the 49ers' wideout corps Week 4 against Denver depending on the status of No. 1 wideout Mike Evans (ribs/oblique). If Evans can't play against the Broncos, both Cowing and Jordan Watkins figure to see a rise in their offensive snap counts. However, Cowing was held without a catch (on two targets) this past Sunday against Arizona even with Evans exiting in the second quarter, so fantasy managers may not be able to count on Cowing for increased production even with more opportunity. Adding to that context is the fact that the Broncos have a tough pass defense that has limited WRs to 18.4 fantasy points per game this season, 10th-best in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Kacmarek was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. Kacmarek is a massive, strong blocking tight end who won't see much receiving work in the pros. He's likely to play a lot of snap as a rookie considering Miami's shaky roster, but Greg Dulcich is expected to operate as the team's top pass-catcher at the tight end position. Kacmarek is no more than the deepest of deep sleepers.

Daniels was selected by the Rams in the sixth round of April's draft. It helped that he played in 68 games across six seasons at Liberty, LSU and Miami, but Daniels ranked third in this WR rookie class in receiving yards (2,991) and second in TD receptions (28) for his career. His overall efficiency was good, though he failed to emerge as anything more than a secondary target once he left Liberty. Daniels will battle for a roster spot and is no more than a dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Homer and the Steelers take on the division rival Bengals at home in Week 3. He rushed twice for 16 yards after filling in for Rico Dowdle, who was forced out of the contest with a toe injury. With Dowdle questionable to play against Cincinnati, Homer could be elevated into a backup role once again. He was reverted to the practice squad on Monday, but he's expected to be back on Pittsburgh's roster for Sunday's contest. However, as long as Jaylen Warren is healthy, Homer's role will be limited against the Bengals first-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Travis Homer and the Steelers travel to take on the Browns in Week 4. He recorded one carry for no gain and was not targeted during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3 as Jaylen Warren's backup. With Rico Dowdle (toe) in jeopardy of missing his second straight contest, Homer is in line for the No. 2 RB role once again. However, Warren should handle the bulk of touches out of the backfield versus Cleveland's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Nowakowski was selected by the Steelers in the fifth round of April's draft. Nowakowski is a bit undersized with very small hands, but he's a capable blocker and, after totaling 18 catches in 36 games at Wisconsin, made a little bit of a leap as a pass catcher in 2025 (his lone season at Indiana), posting a 32-387-2 receiving line. He's expected to play fullback and offer some tight end depth behind Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington.

Rudolph is expected to return as the clipboard holder in Pittsburgh, with Aaron Rodgers back as the starter. The veteran quarterback has never appeared in more than 10 games in a single season and made just one start in 2025 (he threw for 171 yards and one TD on 31 attempts). Rudolph has thrown 30 touchdowns and 22 interceptions in his six-year career, and isn't much of a rushing threat (career 75-209-1). The 31-year-old wouldn't even be a QB2 option in superflex if called on to start.

Green was selected by the Browns in the sixth round of April's draft. Green is a huge, aggressive dual-threat quarterback. He's a major threat with his legs (112-999-8 rushing last season) but a work in progress as a passer, as he completed only 61% of his passes and threw 11 INTs on only 326 attempts in 2025. Green's size and athleticism (which included a 4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) supplies him with massive upside, but he'll need to improve as a passer in order to find a starting opportunity. He'll continue to compete for playing time with Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel.

Klein was selected by the Texans in the second round of April's draft. He's an inexperienced, blocking tight end who posted an ugly 5.5 YPT and 57.6% catch rate in his collegiate career. Klein peaked with a 24-248-1 receiving line in 2025 and now joins a Texans' offense that already includes Dalton Schultz, Cade Stover and Foster Moreau at the tight end position. Klein may be Houston's tight end of the future, but he won't be on the fantasy radar as a rookie.

outlooksByWeek.4: Alec Ingold took advantage of a rash of tight end injuries to catch three of four targets for 35 yards in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills. The veteran fullback has yet to get a carry this season, but his blocking ability makes him a better fit to handle the kinds of assignments Charlie Kolar and David Njoku were getting in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, rather than receiving TE Oronde Gadsden. Ingold has shown some aptitude as a pass catcher in the past, but his primary role will still be to protect Justin Herbert and open holes for the running game. Ingold will be a TD-dependent dart throw in Week against a Seahawks defense that has given up 14 receptions to RBs this season, tied for 17th in the league, and which has allowed a combined three receiving touchdowns to RBs and TEs through three games.

Kameron Johnson is expected to play a depth role in the Buccaneers' receiving corps during the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. The third-year wideout has played just six offensive snaps through Tampa Bay's first three games this season. However, he's expected to have more opportunities in the near future, with Jalen McMillan (knee) set to miss time. Despite the increased opportunities, Johnson will likely struggle finding fantasy value, as he'll likely operate as the team's WR4 without Baker Mayfield (thumb) at the helm. The matchup is favorable, though, as Green Bay's defense has allowed 8.6 yards per target to wideouts this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jimmy Horn will likely play a minimal offensive role in the Panthers' Week 2 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 22.4 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1. Horn had a poor Week 1 performance despite not receiving an offensive touch, as the second-year wideout had a costly fumble on a punt return that helped set up a Bears touchdown. He's not expected to see much volume or be very involved in Carolina's offensive game plan going forward, especially with the emergence of Jalen Coker (ankle). Horn is also in for a tough divisional matchup in Week 2, with the Falcons' defense allowing just 6.5 yards per target to WRs last week.

player.seasonOutlook: Shavers tore his ACL in the playoffs and is unlikely to make a fantasy impact once back on the field in 2026.

Boerkircher was selected by the Jaguars in the second round of April's draft. Boerkircher is a blocking tight end who handled a 3% target share (lowest in this rookie TE class) across 52 collegiate games (five seasons). He aligned in the slot 30% of the time and posted a 1.04 YPRR, both of which are lowest in this TE group. He'll file in as a blocking complement to starter Brenton Strange and is not a fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.4: Ke'Shawn Williams and the Bengals play host to the Jaguars in Week 4. He played no offensive snaps but generated 131 yards on five kick returns on special teams during Cincinnati's Week 3 loss and also lost a fumble. Williams remains off the fantasy radar, but with Colbie Young (knee) and Andrei Iosivas (thumb/IR) set to miss the contest against Jacksonville, he could earn some additional opportunities as a fourth receiver.

player.seasonOutlook: Leonard is expected to operate as the Colts' No. 2 quarterback this season. It's a notable designation, as starter Daniel Jones continues to recover from a torn Achilles suffered in Week 14 last season. Should Jones miss time to begin the 2026 season, Leonard is positioned to start. Leonard made one start as a rookie, throwing for 270 yards and two touchdowns and rushing for 21 yards and an additional score, primarily against Houston's backup defense in Week 18. The 2025 sixth-round pick adds value with his legs, but he'd be no more than a fringe QB2 even if called on to start.

Miller was selected by the Patriots in the seventh round of April's draft. Miller has decent size, but he has struggled with effectiveness, posting a 4.57 YPC (worst in this rookie class) during his collegiate career (including an ugly 3.88 in 2025). Poor tackle breaking and YAC numbers give him perhaps the worst efficiency profile in this RB class, and he hasn't shown much in the passing game (career 40-336-2 line). He ran a solid 4.42 40-yard dash at the combine but posted the worst marks in this RB class in the vertical and broad jump. He didn't make the initial 53-man roster, but will look to stick on the practice squad.

Cuevas was selected by the Ravens in the fifth round of April's draft. Cuevas wasn't targeted much during three collegiate seasons at Washington and Alabama (57-793-6, 5% target share), but he was effective when called on, averaging 10.4 yards per target. He's a bit of a tweener and underwhelmed athletically at the combine, but can help as a blocker and receiver. He'll battle fellow rookie Matthew Hibner for snaps behind Mark Andrews and Durham Smythe this season.

outlooksByWeek.5: Dareke Young's role in the Raiders' offense could increase as injuries mount in the wide receiver room. The former Seahawk's familiarity with Klint Kubiak hasn't translated into much work as a pass catcher, as he's split his time between special teams and the offense, but he saw multiple targets for the first time in 2026 during a Week 4 loss to Kansas City. With Jack Bech on the shelf due to a fractured forearm and Jalen Nailor now in the concussion protocol, Young could line up as Las Vegas' No. 3 WR in Week 5 against a Patriots secondary that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and could be without top cornerback Christian Gonzalez.

player.seasonOutlook: Nussmeier was selected by the Chiefs in the seventh round of April's draft. Nussmeier is an undersized, pocket quarterback and older prospect. He was extremely conservative last season, posting rookie-class-low marks in aDOT (6.4), YPA (6.7) and YPC (9.9). Aside of his ability to avoid sacks (career 3.40% sack rate), Nussmeier's efficiency isn't overly impressive and he's a nonfactor as a rusher (career 33-179-5 line and a class-low 1.4 carries per game). Nussmeier will handle No. 3 duties behind Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jared Wayne drew seven targets in Week 2 as the Texans played without top WR Nico Collins (hamstring). Wayne could be an option for desperate deep-league fantasy managers in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most points and yards in the league. If Collins sits again, Wayne will join Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, and Jaylin Noel as the only healthy options in Houston's WR room. Wayne caught only two of his seven targets in Week 2 against the Bengals, and he has only 65 career receiving yards in six games across three seasons in Houston.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jared Wayne has caught only four of 12 targets for 65 yards heading into Houston's Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. The third-year pro has had opportunities in the absence of Nico Collins (hamstring), but even if Collins remains sidelined in Week 4, Wayne hasn't shown much to suggest he deserves consideration for fantasy lineups. Wayne has yet to score a TD in his career, and only three of the Cowboys' 10 total TDs allowed this season have been scored by WRs.

outlooksByWeek.5: Sterling Shepard hasn't factored in the Jets' minimal passing game ahead of a Week 5 tilt against the Browns. Shepard has just one target over two weeks since being elevated from the practice squad, seemingly overtaking Malik McClain for the team's fourth receiver role. In an offense that can sustain two receivers at most, Shepard appears unlikely to pop against a defense that's allowing 8.8 yards per target to opposing wide outs.

player.seasonOutlook: Joly was selected by the Broncos in the fifth round of April's draft, but was later waived and claimed by Miami. Joly is a highly productive receiving tight end who ranked near the top of this rookie TE class in all receiving counting stats (166-1,978-15) and target share (17%) during 50 collegiate games at UConn and NC State. He's not much of a blocker, but he could stretch the seam as a move tight end in the pros. Joly may one day emerge as a receiving option, but it's going to take some time.

Virgil was selected by the Cardinals in the fifth round of April's draft. Virgil is a tall, thin, perimeter, vertical receiver who ranked near the top of this WR rookie class in aDOT (14.7) and YPR (15.8) but near the basement in RAC (4.5), catch rate (54%) and YPRR (1.79) during his career at Miami Ohio and Texas Tech. A class-high 48% of his targets came on deep routes, though he played a more well-rounded role in 2025 -- his lone season with the Red Raiders. Virgil ran a 4.57 40-yard dash at 187 pounds at the combine, which works out to a poor speed score of 86. Virgil will battle Kendrick Bourne for No. 3 duties behind Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson. He's off the short-term fantasy radar.

Burks was selected by the Colts in the seventh round of April's draft. Burks is a small receiver who has experience as both a primary perimeter receiver (under 25% slot in 2023 and 2025) and a primary slot (over 80% slot in 2022 and 2024). He had productive seasons at both Purdue and Oklahoma, though his overall efficiency is fairly poor across the board. That includes an ugly 6.4 YPT and 1.37 YPRR, both of which rank near the basement of this rookie WR class. He showed very well athletically at the combine, including a 4.30 40-yard dash and class-best marks in the vertical (42.5) and bench press (26 reps). Burks is a longshot for 2026 fantasy value.

Law was selected by the Lions in the fifth round of April's draft. Law is a short-area/slot target who played a limited role in three seasons at Alabama (33 catches in 34 games) prior to delivering a 53-540-3 receiving line at Kentucky last season. Law's career 4.2 aDOT is lowest in this WR rookie class, but his 9.1 RAC and 78% catch rate rank first. He'll battle for a returner/depth receiver role and isn't a fantasy option.

Henderson was selected by the Seahawks in the sixth round of April's draft. Henderson is a thin receiver with small hands who has experience playing inside and out (career 38% slot rate). A converted running back, Henderson was limited to five catches in three seasons at Alabama prior to making a leap to a 45-766-5 receiving line (22% target share) in his lone season at Kansas. Henderson was cut in late August and will attempt to work his way back onto an active roster.

Koziol was selected by the Jaguars in the fifth round of April's draft. Across 49 collegiate games at Houston and Ball State, Koziol produced 349 targets, 237 receptions, 2,234 yards, 24 TDs, a 23% target share and a 24% air yard share. All six stats easily top this TE rookie class and that production included a massive 94-839-8 showing in 2024. Koziol has work to do as a blocker, but his size and production suggest there's clear receiving upside. He's worth stashing in dynasty, but doesn't have a path to short-term value behind Brenton Strange and likely fellow rookie Nick Boerkircher.

Carr reportedly considered a return after sitting out the 2025 season, but did not end up signing with a team. He played pretty well during his two-year run with the Saints (including finishing in the top 12 in completion percentage, YPA and QBR in 2024), but injuries cost him seven games in 2024 and he remained an underwhelming fantasy option. Even after a strong start to that 2024 season (21-plus fantasy points in Weeks 1 and 2), Carr ended up contributing 15.1 fantasy PPG in 10 games, which ranked 19th for the season. Incredibly, that matches his best fantasy showing since his career-best 10th in 2016. Carr is a solid passer, but he simply doesn't run enough (below 110 yards in four straight seasons, with one TD during the span) to provide high-end fantasy output.

Royer was selected by the Browns in the fifth round of April's draft. After barely seeing the field during three seasons at Ohio State, Royer broke out with a 50-522-3 receiving line (21% target share) in 2024, prior to dipping to 29-416-4 (10%) in 2025. He has solid size with big hands and could emerge as a versatile depth option. Once back on the field, he'll compete for reps behind Harold Fannin Jr. this season.
